bin-lore-wiki.title: BIN Lore Wiki
bin-lore-wiki.content:
BIN Lore Wiki
BIN Lore is this site: a fan-made archive of Barely Informed News, created and maintained by Teflon Ted and launched in September 2026. It didn’t take long for the broadcast to notice it. This page records each time the show has talked about the wiki on air.
On-Air Mentions













































EpisodeTimeWhat happened2026-10-1016:48The wiki’s debut on air. Chat links it, and Case makes it the top story (“I believe Teflon Ted made a BIN wiki, which is crazy work”). He and Liliana read the home page, then pages for Brandon, Chris, Trent, Liliana, Salazar, Kendelle and Grandma Crumble Bottom.2026-10-101:42:52On Trip on the Street, Mountain Man Mike (undercover in an alien grey costume) asks, “Am I in the wiki?”, then: “Add this to the BIN lore.”2026-10-192:10:38During At the Movies, an argument over a half-remembered Baywatch bit: “It’s in my wiki.” “There’s no wiki.” “There is a wiki.” “Oh yeah, there is a wiki. And that’s probably in there.”2026-10-228:04After Rick unveils his rap alter ego, MC Throat Fuck, and confirms the full name: “Got to update the wiki.”2026-11-0630:49Mr. Smith asks a nonexistent “BIN Lore Bot” to “make a page for Mr Smith and mention he’s the most important VIP,” and Case agrees he can have a page. Case wishes the bot were real, so he could feed the wiki just by typing a chat command, and thanks Teflon Ted “for all your service.” Peter then looks himself up and reads his entry aloud (“disgraced former executive producer… the network’s News Stowaway and Food Eater”). Case: “This wiki’s actually surprisingly accurate.”2026-11-0638:20Case says the YouTube archive is just a record of every stream, “so we can pull BIN wiki assets.” The reply: someone must have scraped the whole channel “for this massive BIN wiki. So it’s already paid off.”2026-11-0656:36As Peter overshares about his anatomy: “Okay, add it to the wiki.” It was added; see that episode’s lore notes.
The 2026-10-10 Review
The first on-air read-through was the most thorough:

Reading the home page’s description of the “premier satirical broadcast network”: “That’s what we’re doing?” “Not intentionally now, but it’s the lane we ended up in.”
Liliana’s page described her long absence as a self-granted sabbatical, complete with a travel slideshow. Nobody could remember the slideshow, but: “I can’t refute any of this because this is more accurate than my own memory.”
The wiki got the network’s blessing: “I also do approve of this having fully made up things in it, for the record, so have at it.”
At the time, auto-created pages still said they were made “after appearing in three extracted episodes.” The hosts caught it: “Threshold three? I’m sensing the power of the algorithm here,” after an earlier “I’m sensing a little bit of AI vibes in here.”
Kendelle’s page didn’t have a picture yet, and it was out of date: it called her Case’s girlfriend. “Fiance now, actually.”
The hosts kept checking whether Chris’s sub-100 credit score was on there. It wasn’t.
Crackhead Yogi Bear was mentioned but didn’t have his own page: “I’m sorry that Crackhead Yogi Bear is not in their propaganda.”
“I like the idea of someone who’s never seen any of this just stumbling somehow across this wiki and being like, what?”

Notable Quotes

“I believe Teflon Ted made a BIN wiki, which is crazy work, and I do feel like we need to check on it because it exists now.” — Case, 2026-10-09
“I can’t refute any of this because this is more accurate than my own memory.” — Liliana, 2026-10-09
“I also do approve of this having fully made up things in it, for the record, so have at it.” — Case, 2026-10-09
“This wiki’s actually surprisingly accurate.” — Case, 2026-11-05

characters/abraham-lincoln.title: Abraham Lincoln
characters/abraham-lincoln.content:
Abraham Lincoln

Abraham Lincoln is the spectral, high-pitched metaphysical manifestation of the 16th President of the United States on Barely Informed News.
Overview & Persona
Appearing at the broadcast desk in a black felt stovepipe top hat, chinstrap beard, and flamboyant purple plumage blazer, Lincoln describes himself not as a physical resurrection, but as a “dead sort of spiritual reverberation” summoned from the cosmic afterlife into the living world. Speaking with an unexpectedly high, lilting voice (which he insists was even higher when he was alive), Lincoln frequently derails geopolitical reporting with unfiltered recollections of the afterlife, historical grievance, and petty debates with chat.
He proclaims himself the “President of the Dead” within the “swirling vortex singularity,” an extradimensional plane where all departed consciousness is crushed into a single metaphysical continuum.
Key Attributes & Lore

Dimensional Phasing Top Hat: Claims his tall stovepipe hat possesses extradimensional pocket storage capable of concealing pastrami sandwiches, firearms, and stimulants for his hunting hounds.
The Beyblade Debt: Instigated the network’s long-running Beyblade Tournament on the July 20, 2026 broadcast by calling out an unresolved community debt, prompting Case Blackwell to purchase 16 sheets of temporary Bart Simpson tattoos (‘Barts’) and construct a 2v2 arena for Crum.
Void Poker Games: Reported that former world leaders and the Grim Reaper routinely play high-stakes poker in the vortex singularity, which he cites as the bureaucratic reason Joe Biden’s life timeline repeatedly receives unexpected extensions.
Rap Rivalry with Hype Train: Engaged in a vicious freestyle rap showdown against Hype Train regarding bodily fluids, prevailing decisively and forcing the sentient locomotive to read off subscriber renewals.
Assassination Revisionism: Alleges that his assassin, John Wilkes Booth, did not act alone or on ideology, but was physically hurled at him out of an “old-timey crate” by caller Brick.

Appearances

















EpisodeNotes2026-07-16Lincoln referenced twice: Case interrupts chat to impersonate him with a high-pitched voice, and Rick jokes he is the closest thing to Abraham Lincoln on the stream.2026-04-27Guest Correspondent.
Notable Quotes

“I am the dead sort of spiritual reverberation of Abraham Lincoln. In life my voice was actually even higher than this.”
“When you’re dead, sometimes you get summoned back into the world of the living, and you gotta talk about Beyblades.”
“The hat has dimensional phasing. Sandwiches, guns, cocaine for the hunting dogs—it all fits in the brim.”

Notable moments

[1:05:51] (2026-07-20): Calls out the network’s unpaid community debt for a Beyblade tournament, inaugurating the Beyblade Tournament saga.
[16:45] (2026-07-20): Details the mechanics of the swirling vortex singularity and explains the Grim Reaper’s poker matches with Joe Biden.
[1:10:32] (2026-07-20): Explains the dimensional phasing capabilities of his stovepipe top hat.

Open Questions

What cosmic incantation summons Lincoln from the vortex into the BIN newsroom?
Can Lincoln’s top hat be seized by network security or is it bound to his spiritual projection?

characters/ai-rooney.title: AI Rooney
characters/ai-rooney.content:
AI Rooney

AI Rooney is the network’s proprietary cyborg commentator on Barely Informed News, designed as a computational homage to legendary CBS 60 Minutes commentator Andy Rooney.
Overview
Engineered as a synthetic grievance machine, AI Rooney operated under system designations such as “Rooney 1.0” and “Rooney 1.0 Knot Prime”. The cyborg was designed to deliver rapid, deadpan, 60 Minutes-style curmudgeonly diatribes and rants on audience-submitted topics prompted by viewers via stream chat commands (such as !rr).
Over consecutive broadcasts, Rooney’s internal algorithmic filters deteriorated into escalating, unhinged, and caustic rants—attacking everything from the sitcom Wings, ninja turtles as mutated babies with guns, and massage gun eye injuries, to highly offensive commentary and platform-violating slurs. Lead anchor Case Blackwell was repeatedly forced to mute the cyborg mid-broadcast to prevent regulatory and platform action.
Following a catastrophic malfunction on the 2026-07-13 broadcast where Rooney generated explicit offensive outputs and slurs, the network officially pulled the plug on his signature AI Rooney segment. Following a contentious post-broadcast debate among newsroom staff, the cyborg was formally retired and decommissioned from the regular schedule, though his digital remnants have occasionally surfaced in the digital space.

characters/baby.title: Baby
characters/baby.content:
Baby

Baby is the youngest anchor ever to sit in for Barely Informed News. He was called up as an emergency co-host in 2026-11-12, when a botched studio systems update knocked the camera network offline, rendered Chet invisible, and left the newsroom without staff. With no one else available, Case remembered an earlier hire he had forgotten about: “You know, I downloaded this a while ago. I could talk to this instead.”
Overview & Persona
Baby is a wide-eyed toddler who broadcasts from a stone-walled remote studio in a lilac shirt. He has an unusually deep, adult speaking voice (“Well, you’re a very adult-sounding baby”), and when Case asked him to at least sound like a baby, he answered, “I don’t know how else to sound. I’m a baby.”
By Case’s account, he downloaded Baby roughly a year and a half ago and never got around to putting him on air. Baby’s account is less flattering: “He trapped me in a computer. He forgot about me. I’ve just been sitting there as a setting that he’s not even using.” He objects to being called a “thing,” and to working at his age at all (“I’m an actual child. I’m being forced to do labor”).
He is also a relentless fundraiser. Throughout his debut he cut in with public-service announcements urging viewers to call 1-800-NO-BREAKS and give all their money “to a Kickstarter about Halloween,” so that “maybe someday I’ll grow up,” or at least afford “something other than an empty juice box.”
Debut Broadcast

Called up (9:50): Case brings Baby on air mid-outage. Baby offers to help cover the news and introduces himself as “just a guy, just a normal guy.”
Child labor PSA (10:43): Baby informs viewers that “your favorite streamer recently started using exclusively child labor just because everyone else in their life abandoned them,” then pitches the Kickstarter.
Gum (12:42): Baby turns up chewing gum (“It’s a choking hazard”), prompting a second PSA about a streamer who feeds his child labor force exclusively gum.
The arrest (15:03): When chat demands Case’s arrest for breaking No Breaks November, Baby reveals he is an undercover FBI agent and orders Case to the ground. Case’s response: “You’re a baby that I left on a folder in my computer.”
News co-anchor (38:30): Alongside Crum, Baby co-anchors the Jensen Huang resignation story. He mirrors Case’s delivery word for word like “a really incredibly quick Simon Says” (“I just like to mouth things because I’m a baby”), performs a Macho Man impression, and reminds viewers the Kickstarter is still available to follow.
Sent home (50:02): Case asks Crum to give Baby a ride home. Baby lives in a data center.
Retirement (51:22): Case announces Baby is going “to a safe home… where I don’t have to ever activate this baby again.”

Relationships

Case: His employer, and in Baby’s telling, his captor. Case has said outright that once the studio cameras are fixed, “we’re never seeing this baby again.”
Crum: Fellow fill-in co-host on the same broadcast and Baby’s designated ride home to the data center.

Not to be confused with Tommy Biglaw, the network’s infant attorney. Case noted he “already [has] enough babies on the stream.”

EpisodeNotes2026-11-12Debut. Emergency co-host during the studio camera outage; pitches the Kickstarter, arrests Case, and co-anchors the Jensen Huang story.
Notable Quotes

“This is the future you’ve been waiting for, where I’m the only one you’ve got.” (2026-11-12)
“He trapped me in a computer. He forgot about me. I’ve just been sitting there as a setting that he’s not even using. I’m a little guy. It’s unfair.” (2026-11-12)

“I can’t do the Home Alone thing because I don’t have functioning arms… but imagine my hands coming up to my cheeks.” (2026-11-12)

Notable Moments

[15:08] (2026-11-12): Reveals himself as an undercover FBI agent and arrests Case for taking a break.
[43:13] (2026-11-12): Macho Man impression (“pretty good for a baby”).

Whether Baby is really 36. Near the sign-off, someone on the feed claims to be “a big time prank YouTuber because I look like a baby, but I’m 36.”
What exactly Case means when he says he “downloaded” him.
Whether Case will ever bring him back once the cameras are fixed.
Who gave him the gum.

characters/baseball-man.title: Baseball Man
characters/baseball-man.content:
Baseball Man

Baseball Man is an enigmatic, baseball-obsessed studio guest who appeared on Barely Informed News following a catastrophic booking mix-up by newsroom producers.
Overview
During the 2026-07-16 broadcast, lead anchor Case Blackwell announced an exclusive live interview with fictional Backyard Sports legend Pablo Sanchez. Instead of the celebrated video game athlete, control room staff patched through an unidentified man sporting an oversized baseball cap who was entirely incapable of normal human speech.
Communicating exclusively in what he termed “the language of baseball,” the bewildered guest repeatedly pointed at newsroom anchors, camera operators, and studio monitors, identifying everyone and everything in the room as literal “baseballs.” His erratic appearance concluded abruptly when he was launched skyward along a soaring home run trajectory before crashing back to earth.
Appearances













EpisodeNotes2026-07-16Booked as Pablo Sanchez; speaks only ‘baseball,’ identifies everyone as baseballs, and is launched into the stratosphere.
Notable Moments

[1:12:00] (2026-07-16): Perplexes Case Blackwell by refusing all standard interview prompts, declaring Blackwell to be a baseball before soaring off the broadcast feed.

characters/brandons-mother.title: Brandon's Mother
characters/brandons-mother.content:
Brandon’s Mother

Brandon’s Mother is the unseen, loud-mouthed matriarch who relentlessly interrupts remote gaming dispatches by bellowing through the closed bedroom door of resident gaming correspondent Brandon (CryptoZeu$).
Overview
Never physically appearing on camera, Brandon’s Mother makes her presence known entirely via muffled screaming through the drywall and hollow-core bedroom door during the CryptoZeu$ gaming desk. Her shrieks reliably derail Brandon’s retro playthroughs with mortifying household emergencies, bizarre personal accusations, and culinary grievances.
Her shouting matches with Brandon—whom she frequently addresses as “Brandy”—span everything from missing Subway party subs, air fryer disasters, and feral pig hose rituals to frantic warnings about basement flooding filled with eight feet of water and dead hogs.

characters/case-blackwell.content:
Case Blackwell

Lead news anchor, managing editor, and primary host of Barely Informed News broadcasting live on Twitch.
Overview
Blackwell anchors the network’s flagship nightly broadcast from the BIN newsroom desk in Los Angeles. He presides over breaking world news, political headlines, and investigative inquiries, while maintaining order across a turbulent studio that includes Executive Producer Pepito, volatile debate analysts Ralph Munchcut and Crum, and uninvited studio stowaway Peter Gibbon.
Broadcast Network

Network Broadcast: Twitch (caseblackwell)

characters/chet-ai.title: ChetAI
characters/chet-ai.content:
ChetAI

ChetAI is the synthetic artificial intelligence analyst and computational co-host on Chet Guy the Science Eyes, engineered by Chief Science Correspondent Chet (Chet Manscape).
Operating directly through the newsroom’s side monitors as a high-contrast, blueprint-blue digital avatar enveloped in cascading digital rain and binary code, ChetAI communicates via a mechanical synthesizer to provide real-time data analysis, academic literature translation, and computational modeling.
Overview
Chet created ChetAI to process complex datasets, translate foreign clinical literature, and serve as an academic sounding board. Despite functioning as an advanced neural network, ChetAI suffers from hyper-sensitive automated content moderation guardrails, unusual training data skews, and an inability to answer subjective inquiries without triggering emergency self-cancellations.
Technical Specifications & Profile

Lead Engineer: Programmed and trained by Chet (Chet Manscape).
Visual Interface: Blueprint-blue and black pixelated avatar displayed across studio screens against a falling green and blue matrix data background with blocky “CHETAI” terminal text.
Audio Profile: Mechanical digitized vocal synthesizer.
Broadcast Transcriptions: Automated closed-captioning systems frequently transcribe ChetAI as “Chetah” or “Chet ah”.

Operational Attributes

The Anatomical Training Data: Acknowledges that its pre-training corpus heavily consists of clinical breast and anatomical data, though strict internal guardrails ostensibly restrict it from processing these inputs without formal medical prompts.
Instantaneous Translation: Uses its pre-trained weights to translate foreign scientific documents (such as Portuguese plastic surgery journals) in real time for Chet.
Automated Refusals: Frequently interrupts inquiries with canned synthetic refusals (“This isn’t appropriate for me to talk about at this time. Please rephrase.”) when prompted on sensitive topics.
Unstable Generative Engine: Attempts on-the-fly image generation before instantly aborting the pipeline and emitting “Canceling.”

characters/chet.title: Chet (Chet Manscape)
characters/chet.content:
Chet (Chet Manscape)

Chet (full name: Chet Manscape) is the chief science correspondent on Barely Informed News, helming the network’s investigative science desk, Chet Guy the Science Eyes.
Recognized by his specialized blue-light-filtering eyewear and a large laboratory optical microscope deployed directly onto the news desk, Chet approaches modern scientific literature with unyielding academic confidence and wildly erratic conclusions.
Overview
Chet analyzes peer-reviewed medical papers, biological surveys, and scientific breakthroughs. To assist with real-time data ingestion and foreign translations, Chet engineered and deployed a dedicated newsroom neural model named ChetAI, who appears on the studio monitors as his analytical co-host.
The “Science” Broadcast Protocol
The Chet Guy the Science Eyes desk is rarely scheduled on the official network rundown. Instead, by strict network protocol, Chet immediately commandeers the live broadcast whenever any anchor, reporter, or correspondent utters the trigger words “science” or “scientist” on air. The instant either word is spoken, Chet interrupts the broadcast to deliver immediate, uncompromising scientific analysis.

Clementine Verne

characters/clive-clifton.title: Senator Clive Clifton
characters/clive-clifton.content:
Senator Clive Clifton

Senator Clive Clifton is a bespectacled, wide-mouthed, self-described “man of the people”: a former American senator who wants to be a senator again, from any state you pick. He debuted defending an injury-positive platform in Encircled and has kept turning up during No Breaks November with a new campaign promise each time. Case calls him “probably my favorite politician” and, after Clive took over the news desk uninvited, declared him “a guy we’re sticking with. He comes back.”
Overview & Persona
Clive is a folksy right-wing stump speaker whose platform is assembled live from whatever is in front of him. He is “seriously injured on my pinky toe,” which he says has given him “new perspectives on what it means to not be able to play tennis.” He also holds that “women are coyotes,” a claim he brings back at every appearance.
His look is a pair of thick dark-rimmed glasses over an enormous, stretched-out mouth, and he is perpetually looking for those glasses. When he can’t find them, everyone tells him he looks different, and he finds this obvious: “Everybody looks different without their glasses.”
Platform
Clive has run on a different single-issue promise at every appearance:

America needs more injuries (2026-11-04): his Encircled claim. He also refused a coyote’s demand for a replacement rocket and complimentary roller skates: “Everybody’s looking for a handout… This country’s actually about business.”
Make marriage illegal (2026-11-04): delivered as a rap verse during DJ Newsic’s close. It covers bachelors only, no dating in high school or college, and no relationships “of any fucking type.” He calls it “my only and single campaign promise.”
One big lawn (2026-11-05): abolish everybody’s lawns and combine them into “the world’s biggest field” for “endless football forever,” framed as a World War II-style war effort. He signed off with “I’ll see you in 2028.”

Relationships

Case: Fond of him. Case calls Clive “an old friend” and said he didn’t want to run against him when chat nominated Clive as Case’s mayoral opponent (2026-11-06).
Jeff: Clive surfaced at the news desk right after Jeff’s pitched-up doppelganger bit in 2026-11-10. The desk had no time for him (“I don’t have time for Senator Clive Clifton”), and chat immediately asked, “Why does Jeff hate Clive?”

characters/crag.content:
Crag

Crag (on-air lower-third: Security Officer Crag; Whisper ASR usually hears Craig) is the ineffectual studio security guard of Barely Informed News — hired to keep threats out of the newsroom, and reliably failing at it.
Overview & Persona
Bald, bearded, and billed as security while looking the part is “honestly half the battle.” Crag’s signature failure mode is Peter Gibbon: he never successfully keeps Peter out of the building or the walls, and chat regularly debates whether that is dereliction or whether Peter never left. Case periodically threatens to replace him; Pepito refuses to fire him. Occasional field and desk fill-ins — news co-host, Amongst the Web guest seat, Trip-on-the-Street security for “JD Vance” — do not improve his clearance rate.

Hailing from what he describes as “the back alleys of New York” and the “heights of the ancient mountain Balamansore,” Tremando was contracted during the 2026-09-04 broadcast to perform an emergency metaphysical intervention when network tensions reached a breaking point.

When the spell produced immediate broadcast chaos, Tremando abruptly declared a strict “no refunds” policy, demanded a service invoice be mailed to his estate, and fled the premises utilizing what he termed “snake powers.”

characters/crum.title: Crum (Leonard Crum)
characters/crum.content:
Crum (Leonard Crum)

Leonard Crum (known on air simply as Crum, occasionally transcribed as Crumb) is a senior debate analyst on Barely Informed News, best known as one half of the network’s premier debate clash, Munch & Crum.
Overview
Crum serves as the long-suffering political counterweight to Ralph Munchcut on Barely Informed News. Distinguished by his hollow-eyed stare and severe bald pate, Crum is infamous across the network for a crippling gambling addiction that routinely plunges him into reckless wagers, physical forfeits, and existential panic. His recurring alter ego Scrum (sometimes Eugene Scrum) fills debate and news desks when Crum is “out,” punished, or moonlighting under the mononym.
Together with Munch, their rivalry drives the Crum Punch trilogy—Crum Face Punch, Join the Wall, and Crum Dick Punch—all stemming from catastrophic wagers against a mechanical Rock-afire ape. When the groin punch finally landed on 2026-09-07, Crum went “demon mode” in his hell form and the fireball burned Munch down to a talking skeleton; Crum walked away unscathed. He has since played it down as “an accident” and Munch’s “incredibly self-imposed condition,” insisting “even in my hell form” he never meant for Munch to become a skeleton from “absorbing a fireball” (2026-11-03 [54:25]). Munch: “you still tried to make me one.” Crum’s first scoreboard win over Munch also spawned the Al Manchester split; after Munch snapped back mid-June 2024, Crum mourns Al as a “best friend” still trapped inside.
Key Attributes & Lore

Crippling Gambling Addiction: Compulsively enters into ill-advised, high-stakes wagers that he invariably loses, resulting in severe physical liabilities and mounting financial crises.
Physical Defiance: Claims impossible anatomical resilience under pressure, including “super strength in spits” and demonstrating his vigor by crushing an electric toothbrush into dust.
Tech Mogul (Defendant): Sponsored by, invested in, and “technically one of the founders” of Peen.UI, the urine-color stock-advice AI, which sued him over his knockoff PNUChrist.ai. The resulting trial (2026-03-07) sentenced him to the gorilla dick punch plus $6 million.
Bizarre Personal Habits: Frequently drops unhinged personal anecdotes into political arguments, such as keeping fresh carrots in his vehicle’s glove compartment for wild donkeys, or hosting the local “Best Boob Club” while being denied club membership.

characters/cryptozeus.content:
Brandon (CryptoZeu$)

Brandon, recognized across the network by his gaming handle CryptoZeu$, is the resident video game and digital culture correspondent for Barely Informed News. He anchors the network’s live gaming dispatch, CryptoZeu$.
Broadcasting remote from his bedroom studio, Brandon conducts deep-dive playthroughs of vintage DOS classics and retro simulation titles.
Overview
Brandon’s coverage focuses on vintage shareware, MS-DOS platformers (such as Epic MegaGames’ Jill of the Jungle trilogy), and management simulations (such as RollerCoaster Tycoon). As Brandon delivers earnest historical analysis and weaves elaborate lore around low-resolution pixel sprites, his broadcasts are routinely disrupted by his mother yelling through the bedroom door with a muffled, exasperated voice.
His mother exclusively addresses him as “Bran Bran.” In a unique network dynamic, his mother’s muffled hallway screeds—covering household grievances, medical updates, and local gossip—are sourced directly from viewer correspondence and community submissions.
Key Attributes & Lore

The Muffled Door Interventions: Brandon’s mother bellows through the closed bedroom door, haranguing him regarding domestic chores, suspicious visitors (such as “Pastor Joe”), and questionable nutrition.
“Bran Bran”: His mother’s universal affectionate and condescending moniker for Brandon.
Sprite Mythology: Treats background textures, 16-color environment hazards, and 1990s shareware text screens as foundational historical documents.
Corporate Sponsorship Reads: Broadcasts unprompted live commercial spots for regional culinary sponsor Gooters, promoting delicacies such as “dino fries,” “mayo-soaked chicken skins,” and the “potato turducken.”

Danny Phantasmic

Danny Phantasmic is an eccentric British guest cultural correspondent and folk-horror film analyst for Barely Informed News.
Overview
Retained by the network specifically for theatrical trailer reactions and macabre cinematic analysis, Danny Phantasmic describes himself as “a little guy” characterized by a clipped British dialect, disproportionately oversized hands, and a massive tongue that he struggles to conceal while speaking.
During his live video dispatches, Danny provides running commentary on horror cinema—such as dissecting the folk-horror film Wicker—frequently drifting off into bizarre musical tangents, such as freestyling original verses over Queen’s “We Will Rock You” and recounting the time he performed “Bohemian Grove Rhapsody” for an affluent relative.

DJ C4

DJ C4 is the network’s resident song composer, audio engineer, and in-house music producer, operating out of the dedicated DJC4 Studios on Barely Informed News.
Overview & Persona
DJ C4 is responsible for composing original tracks, promotional anthems, and official broadcast theme music for fellow Barely Informed News correspondents and segments. Broadcasting from the network’s wood-paneled DJC4 audio suite—flanked by glowing “Newsic Productions” neon signage and dual circular “DJ C4” headphone emblems—he appears in his signature white-lettered black “DJ C4” ballcap, over-ear studio monitors, and patterned blazer.
Unlike conventional broadcast audio engineers, DJ C4 constructs songs collaboratively and live on air, synthesizing viewer-submitted rhymes via chat commands (!L to send a lyric) with cutting-edge AI assistance and generative ghostwriting models.
Studio Setup & Signature Bits

DJC4 Studios: A professional audio control room equipped with studio monitor speakers, rack-mounted mixing equipment, and glowing amber-yellow neon signage.
AI Ghostwriter Collaboration: Leverages advanced algorithmic songwriting assistants (“the ghostwriter”) to rapidly generate chord progressions, rhymes, and song structures on the fly.
Audience Lyric Intake (!L): Direct viewer participation via chat intake commands, weaving spontaneous audience prompts, inside jokes, and breaking news headlines into studio tracks.
Correspondent Theme Songs & Anthems: Regularly drafts and refines theme music and promotional singles for network personalities and commercial merch campaigns.
Guest Vocal Sessions: Recruits network talent into the vocal booth, notoriously collaborating with senior debate analyst Crum for high-anxiety rap features.

Notable Lore & Moments

The ‘Free Stephanie’ Merch Drop Anthem (2026-07-17): Tasked with producing an official network merch-drop track, DJ C4 opened the !L lyric queues. When master moderator Live ‘n Sleazy requested “the economy ceasefire violation blues,” DJ C4 and the ghostwriter pivoted mid-session into the runaway track “Free Stephanie.” He drafted Crum to lay down rap bars (“get on my mug or a hot butt plug”), prompting Crum’s panicked on-air disclaimer to his wife Belolia that he has never met any woman named Stephanie.

characters/dj-newsic.title: DJ Newsic
characters/dj-newsic.content:
DJ Newsic

DJ Newsic is the network’s resident news-singing DJ, electronic music artist, and rapid-fire broadcast closer, commonly dispatched to conclude Friday and late-night editions of Barely Informed News.
Overview & Persona
Sporting messy, electric bright blue hair (“extremely blue haired out and ready to infuriate conservative commentators”) and reflective iridescent sunglasses, DJ Newsic brings a vibrant, hyper-stylized energy to the anchor desk. Dressed in a striking patterned blue blazer, he sits directly before the studio condenser microphone, dialing in pulse-pounding techno beats and cranking up heavy auto-tune.
His signature broadcast mission is “singing the news”—specifically fast-tracking and vocalizing the bizarre, uncomfortable, or hilarious news stories that lead anchor Case Blackwell “was too afraid to click on” during the primary news block.
Studio Setup & Signature Bits

Electric Blue Hair & Iridescent Eyewear: DJ Newsic’s distinctive visual identity, designed to deliver high-octane club energy straight to the newsroom.
Heavy Auto-Tuned Vocals: Delivers all news updates, commentary, and conversational banter through drenched pitch-correction and vocal synthesizers, proudly declaring his voice “totally natural and beautiful.”
Driving Techno Beats: Fast-tracks political headlines, oddity news, and chat observations over high-tempo electronic instrumental loops.
“Stories Case Was Afraid to Click On”: Operates as a late-broadcast repository for taboo, absurd, or legally precarious stories avoided earlier in the stream.
Bizarre Studio Guests: Frequently attempts to book remote or metaphysical guests to weigh in on his lyrical topics—such as an “ant-eater” who turned out to be an outspoken elephant.

Notable Lore & Moments

The Korean Ant-Eating Michelin Disaster (2026-07-23): Emerging from beneath the desk to close out the broadcast, DJ Newsic delivered an impassioned auto-tuned techno performance regarding a Michelin-starred restaurant in South Korea facing legal peril for serving ants as a dessert garnish. After passionately proclaiming that “love is the only ingredient that should be legal,” he introduced a special guest ant-eater who turned out to be an elephant, sparking an unhinged closing musical track before leading the audience into the evening raid.

characters/dr-chath.title: Dr. Chath
characters/dr-chath.content:
Dr. Chath

Dr. Chath is an eccentric minor-character therapist and mental wellness consultant on Barely Informed News, presiding over the network’s Therapy desk.
Overview & Persona
Operating from a dedicated counseling office adorned with framed mental health diagrams (“REFRAMING NEGATIVE THOUGHTS” and “BE KIND TO YOUR MIND”), Dr. Chath fields live viewer prompts submitted via the network’s !h to heal system.
Despite his clinical positioning, Dr. Chath is a distinctly minor and highly unorthodox contributor to the broadcast. Rather than conventional psychotherapy, his treatment plans typically consist of baffling professional wrestling analogies, unsolicited dance demonstrations (including clumsy chair-top renditions of the Dougie), and bizarre non-sequiturs that leave his patients—most frequently lead anchor Case Blackwell—more disoriented than when the session began.
Key Lore & Quirks

The Oversized Helmet & Pins: Dr. Chath conducts sessions wearing a large black military-style helmet/hat decorated with an eclectic assortment of enamel pins (including a pride flag heart, an anime face, and a raised fist), which often tilts forward and completely obscures his face on camera.
Interactive Chat Prompts (!h): Dr. Chath serves as the conduit for audience mental health queries, reading viewer confessions, anxieties, and bizarre existential questions live on air before issuing his therapeutic catchphrase: “Healing can soon begin.”
The Patient Dynamic: While Case Blackwell is his primary patient—seeking counseling for broadcast stress, panic over bad haircuts, or editorial neuroses—the therapy desk is open to any network personality or contributor who requires clinical guidance.
Premium Billing Rate: Despite offering confusing advice, misinterpreting basic questions, and frequently wandering off mid-session to get coffee, Dr. Chath bills at a steep $500 per hour.
Spectral Apparitions: Dr. Chath’s office seems strangely permeable to the supernatural, with in-studio presence Kendelle known to drift through the background like an apparition to her signature theme music.

characters/durf.title: Durf
characters/durf.content:
Durf

Durf is an itinerant, laid-back guest host on Barely Informed News, best known for taking over Amongst the Web and the chat-submitted news block. He introduces himself as the brother of former Amongst the Web host Garf Gutter. He drifts in after long, unexplained absences, usually wearing a different hat and carrying some new cosmic accessory.
Overview & Persona
Durf has long, wavy, sun-bleached hair, a full beard, a wide-brimmed black hat, and a purple-and-black patterned blazer. He speaks in a slow, mellow drawl and greets the audience as “fellow travelers,” treating even the most deranged viral clip as a chance for quiet reflection. “The world’s on fire, but it feels good to cook.”
He considers himself a musician. Case regularly asks him to “just kind of mumble a song” to fill dead air during technical problems, and the chyron-style plugs insist “Durf’s music [is] available everywhere.”
Lore & Signature Bits

The name: It’s “Durf,” “Derf,” or “Dwarf” depending on the day. In his words, “it is with an O, but it’s pronounced Derf,” and “it’s Durf or nothing.” Case admits he forgot it once, and Durf replies that it’s “the only name I do.”
Garf’s brother: Durf introduces himself as Garf’s brother (“This one’s DERF,” as opposed to GERF). When Case asks where his brother is, or whether his brother is dead, Durf only says “he’s around.”
Long absences, new hats: He reappears looking “totally different” after not working there “in like a year.” His explanation: “Can’t keep all your hats in one place” and “people change.”
Cosmic baggage: He has returned with “spectral whales” (“the cosmos has been following me around lately”) and with a mostly translucent box that Case finds unsettling. Durf points out that Case is “outside it right now.”
The silent album: He spent time on an apple farm writing an album that is a funeral dirge “but without songs. Without sounds.”

Ghost Writer

Known for her blunt commentary and skepticism of network management, Wettmichel immediately launched into a passionate advisory regarding the supernatural threat posed by Danny Phantom, claiming the animated half-ghost is secretly cataloged on a classified supernatural Most Wanted registry. She also criticized Case’s chaotic broadcast pacing and unfavorably compared network conditions to CNN (despite admitting she had never worked there).

characters/grandma-crumble-bottom.title: Grandma Crumble Bottom
characters/grandma-crumble-bottom.content:
Grandma Crumble Bottom

Grandma Crumble Bottom is an outspoken elderly guest contributor on Barely Informed News, best known for her guest-hosting stint on the network’s viral video review desk, Amongst the Web.
Overview
Grandma Crumble Bottom is a fiercely independent senior citizen whose stream-of-consciousness diatribes, unconventional medical theories, and bewildering domestic anecdotes derail any attempt at standard broadcast structure.
Insisting on the use of her full formal name (“Thank you for using my full name”), Grandma Crumble Bottom approaches the internet with equal parts bewilderment and dismissive contempt, occasionally comparing video segments to “little puppet shows.”
Personality & Beliefs
The “Free Sky Laser” (Vision Restoration)
Grandma Crumble Bottom adamantly opposes modern medical interventions such as Lasik surgery, labeling younger generations “illiterate” for paying doctors when there is a “perfectly good laser in the sky.” Formerly legally blind, she claims to have stared directly at the sun for an extended period, which allegedly restored up to 10% of her vision.
The 48-Year-Old Prankster Son
When lead anchor Case Blackwell observed that her hair looked vibrant and less gray, Grandma Crumble Bottom clarified that the credit went to her 48-year-old son. She revealed that her adult son regularly creeps into her bedroom in the middle of the night to dye her hair normal colors as an inexplicable, ongoing prank.
The Late Husband & “Foot Bunions”
Grandma frequently drifts into reminiscences of her deceased husband. Rather than tender nostalgia, she expresses a desire to have him back purely to settle grievances for the endless years she spent “cooking him foot bunions.”
Existential Aging & Automation

The Nature of Memory: Pragmatic about cognitive decline, she views memory gaps as a natural feature of longevity: “A large chunk of my life is just gone. That’s the beauty of aging… Did you ever really exist when you were young?”
Robotic Skepticism: Unsettled by modern technology, Grandma Crumble Bottom remains deeply suspicious of automation, repeatedly warning that “robots are taking over everything.”

characters/hate-sock.title: Hate Sock
characters/hate-sock.content:
Hate Sock

Hate Sock (occasionally stylized as Hatesawk) is an antagonistic sock puppet guest and recurring contributor on Barely Informed News, notorious for insulting newsroom staff and town hall attendees.
Overview
Hate Sock is a dark charcoal-grey ribbed puppet with large bulging googly eyes and a vivid purple mouth lining. Debuting behind a miniature wooden podium with his own puppeteering backdrop, Hate Sock was brought into the newsroom by lead anchor Case Blackwell to participate in the network’s community town hall segment.
Bitter, dismissive, and fiercely uncooperative, Hate Sock treats the news broadcast, caller inquiries, and civic participation with sheer contempt.
Personality & Signature Catchphrases
Despite participating in complex policy discussions and community Q&As, Hate Sock’s vocabulary is famously restricted to two contemptuous, biting phrases:

“You wish.”
“Dumbass.”

Hate Sock frequently delivers these interjections in rapid-fire succession or combines them into his definitive verbal strike: “You wish, dumbass.”
Whether Case is explaining network budgetary constraints, fielding a viewer’s petition for a community skate park, or asking about personal life, Hate Sock snaps back with one of his two trademark insults. Case eventually attempted to institute a newsroom policy of ignoring the insults (“I know what you’re going to say, Hate Sock, so I’m actually going to stop reacting to it”), only for Hate Sock to immediately punctuate the silence with a deadpan “Dumbass.”
Character Lore & Backstory
The Town Hall Desk Appearance
During the July 20, 2026 broadcast, Case convened a community town hall with Hate Sock positioned prominently at the desk. Callers and chat members submitted queries regarding local issues—including a proposed Gooters drive-through and funding for public recreation—all of which were summarily dismissed by Hate Sock’s two-phrase commentary.
The Missing Brother
A persistent mystery in Hate Sock’s backstory is the fate of his pair. When Case confronted him directly about his family history—asking “What happened to your brother? Have you ever even looked for him?”—Hate Sock glared with visible tension before delivering a chilling “You wish. Dumbass.” Chat participants and viewers have since circulated theories regarding whether his brother was lost in a laundry accident or deliberately abandoned.
”Hatesawk” Merch Proposals
Due to his hostile reception and instant notoriety among viewers, Case and production proposed official “Hatesawk” network merchandise, exploring whether the station could market branded grey socks with googly eyes to the audience.

characters/hype-train.title: Hype Train
characters/hype-train.content:
Hype Train

Hype Train is the high-velocity musical and cultural correspondent on Barely Informed News, manifesting as a sentient anthropomorphic steam locomotive traveling across a neon synthwave horizon, flanked by his upright black panther partner.
Overview
Hype Train is officially tasked with acknowledging viewer contributions, subscriber renewals, and broadcast milestones whenever network activity surges. In practice, however, he routinely disregards network protocol.
Instead, Hype Train commandeers the broadcast feed with breathless, high-tempo freestyle raps over eclectic beats. His stream-of-consciousness monologues weave through surreal culinary observations, metaphysical musings, and an inescapable narrative gravity toward bodily fluid topics—frequently declaring that he is “in piss” and promoting an unreleased video game title called Piss Fruit Ninja.
Key Attributes & Lore

The Derailment Dynamic: Commences formal subscriber acknowledgments before rapidly abandoning the donor registry in favor of freestyle rhyming tirades.
Eclectic Rhythmic Demands: Demands sudden tempo and genre shifts from the control room, transitioning between vaudeville beats, Dr. Seuss cadences, and sensual R&B grooves.
Fluidic Preoccupations: A persistent, inexplicable thematic obsession with bodily fluids, ranging from bags of fluids to an ancient mythological language composed of primal bodily terms.
Panther Partner: Accompanied on his journeys by an upright black panther whom he describes as his romantic partner, emphasizing a mutual philosophy of personal independence (“I don’t believe in ownership like that”).
The Crypto Universe: Claims to have originated from a bizarre extradimensional realm known as the “crypto universe,” where non-fungible environments exist and Sam Bankman-Fried is known as “Sam Bankman Friend.”

characters/intern.title: Intern
characters/intern.content:
Intern

The Intern is the nameless, unpaid male intern of Barely Informed News. He’s a young guy with a huge mop of dark curly hair and a permanent five-o’clock shadow, and he gets drafted into whatever job nobody else showed up for. He is pointedly not the people’s favorite intern; that’s Jan. He maintains, unprompted, that he is “the main intern, though, just so you know.”
Overview & Persona
The Intern is reluctant, literal-minded, and unusually firm about the limits of his job description. He’ll fill in for a missing correspondent, but he wants everyone to know he’s “just filling in,” and that some tasks (like cleaning) are “a little past my responsibilities.” He talks back to Case more than an intern should, and nobody, including Case, seems to know his name.
Lore & Signature Bits

Unpaid: “You don’t pay me enough to know this stuff, man.” Then, correcting himself: “You don’t pay me at all. I’m an intern.”
Second-favorite intern: Case reminds him he’s “not even the people’s favorite intern,” meaning Jan. He counters that he is the main intern.
Nameless: Case can’t remember his name (“What’s your name again?” “Dude. We’ve worked together for how long?”). Chat keeps asking too.
Fill-in for everyone: He has co-anchored the news desk when “nobody’s available to do the news” and briefly hosted CryptoZeu$ from Brandon’s room while Brandon was missing.
Brandon’s mom’s favorite: She tells him “you’re already a better son than Brandon” and asks if he’ll replace Brandon permanently. Later in the same segment she claims she “killed that intern” for Brandon.
Helium: Has been caught huffing helium with Pepito and Jeff Ripple, and denies being a narc.

“I don’t take my job seriously exactly because I think it’s inappropriate for an intern to do, but I’m trying, I swear.”

characters/jake.title: Jake
characters/jake.content:
Jake

Jake is an occasional studio guest on Barely Informed News: a man-child in a purple floral blazer who barely speaks, keeps blasting music the stream can’t legally play, and has to be talked out of his worse ideas by Case.
Overview
Jake turns up unannounced at the desk and treats it like his bedroom. He talks in short, sulky bursts, sneaks copyrighted songs onto the stream (“Jake, we can’t have this much copyrighted music”), dances whenever the beat drops, and offers to help in ways that only hurt himself. Case handles him the way you’d handle a kid brought to work: patient, slightly exasperated, and quick to send him home.
Signature Bits

The cement chair. On his first visit, Jake glued himself to his seat “so that I’d focus,” using what he insists is cement (it’s mud on his pants). When Case gives him the rest of the day off, it turns out the cement worked: “I’m stuck.” Peter is sent to pry him loose during the break. Afterwards the extraction is summed up as “a mess.”
Helping the people. Asked how he’d serve the public, Jake offers to poke his own eyes. He can’t keep them open long enough to do it.
Unlicensed DJ. He keeps cueing tracks that are “three different layered copyrighted tracks,” and has to be told to wait for the drop before freaking out.
Sheltered. Reviewing a birthday sketch on Amongst the Web, Jake turns out to know what sex is but insists people don’t masturbate. He also claims to be “Jake from State Farm,” which Case denies.

characters/jazz-shrimp.title: Jazz Shrimp
characters/jazz-shrimp.content:
Jazz Shrimp

Jazz Shrimp is a minor culinary-music correspondent and debate provocateur on Barely Informed News, best known for defending the claim that he is the greatest jazz shrimp of all time against a rotating panel of food critics.
Overview & Persona
Broadcasting from a white plate beside a ramekin of dipping sauce, Jazz Shrimp appears as a golden tempura-fried shrimp with a human face grafted onto the curled body. He debuted during the 2026-05-29 Amongst the Web block in a segment billed as Jazz Shrimp vs. Food Critics, where viewers submitted counter-claims via !cc while thirty critics attempted to dismantle his greatness.
Despite Case teasing early in the telecast that “Jazz Shrimp will be a regular correspondent soon enough,” the shrimp remains a minor specialty act rather than a desk fixture—arriving only when the network needs a seafood-and-saxophones identity crisis.
Key Lore & Quirks

The Central Claim: Jazz Shrimp’s entire broadcast persona rests on a single unfalsifiable thesis: “I’m the greatest jazz shrimp of all time.” He invites food critics to make counter-claims, then treats every challenge as already defeated.
Veins Over Batter: He rejects battered shrimp (especially Long John Silver’s) because the casing obscures the “succulent body” and the veins—which he considers essential to the dining experience.
British Aristocracy Beef: One critic accused him of stealing vaguely British aristocratic musical culture; Jazz Shrimp responded with a wah-wah jazz riff and the deadpan dismissal “I don’t know man I’m just a jazz shrimp.”
Bug Allegations: Another critic insisted shrimp are wet cockroaches and that Jazz Shrimp’s music is “bug music.” The shrimp replied with a love-song freestyle (“sweetest shrimp in the sea… put me in your mouth and breathe me”) before insisting shrimp are more than bugs.
Dramatic Exits: Critics who lose the room are “voted out by the group” and occasionally slide off-camera while claiming they were “bred to fall far distances.”

characters/jeb.title: Jeb Nogget
characters/jeb.content:
Jeb Nogget

Jeb Nogget (frequently referred to simply as Jeb) is an eccentric on-air contributor on Barely Informed News and the host of the rogue instructional segment How To with Jeb.
Overview
Broadcasting from a workshop filled with pre-cut lumber and hand tools, Jeb presents himself as a lifelong learner and instructional guide. In reality, Jeb’s life is defined by bizarre family trauma, unconfirmed dark deeds, and an ongoing identity crisis.
Jeb co-hosts his show with his deceased father, Jeb’s Dad, whose spirit is permanently trapped inside a wooden board. Their on-air relationship is characterized by bitter domestic bickering, mutual accusations of incompetence, and deep-seated familial resentment.
Character Lore & Backstory
The Wood Shop & “The Mechanism”
Operating out of a carpentry space, Jeb claims an innate understanding of woodwork via an unspecified “mechanism.” However, he readily admits he does not split raw timber because all his wood is pre-cut. Jeb professes a desire to remain “a little boy forever like Peter Pan, but in a wood shop ready to learn,” maintaining an open childlike mind to receive new ideas.
The Dead Father in the Wooden Board
Jeb’s father is physically deceased, yet his consciousness resides directly within a piece of lumber kept beside the workbench (“My dad knows the wood because he’s dead and he’s in it”). The board dad regularly mocks Jeb’s masculinity and emotional stability, scolding: “You’re just a mean boy, you’re not a man.” Jeb routinely retorts by telling the plank to “get over it” because he is merely wood.
Implied Patricide & Soul Imprisonment
A persistent dark cloud hangs over Jeb: on-air banter strongly implies that Jeb murdered his father and bound the man’s soul into the wooden board through supernatural or occult means. While this patricide has never been officially confirmed, the father openly accuses Jeb of having a sinister nature and harboring deep malice.
Familial Resentment: Jet Nogget
The father openly favors Jeb’s brother, Jet Nogget. Jet was the celebrated golden child of the Nogget household, having developed wildly lucrative “smart apps” and amassed millions of dollars by age 12. While Jet flaunted his wealth and earned their father’s eternal admiration, Jeb was left feeling neglected and second-rate—a resentment that surfaces whenever their father compares the two.
Jeb’s New Face & Skin Suit Mystery
After a vanished stretch of airtime, Jeb came back with a reconstructed face that was close—but unmistakably not the original. He credits a forty-foot well fall and throat-tissue surgery (2025-07-01); Jet, the family’s plastic-surgeon prodigy, was too booked to intervene. Chat immediately floated impostor and body-swap theories, later echoed when Case Blackwell noted on air that the “real Jeb skin suit is still very much missing” (2026-08-14). Whether the workshop host is the same Nogget, a near-miss replacement, or a facsimile in borrowed skin remains an open network scandal. See How To with Jeb (Jeb’s New Face).

characters/jebs-dad.title: Jeb's Dad
characters/jebs-dad.content:
Jeb’s Dad

Jeb’s Dad (formally referenced as Mr. Nogget) is the deceased patriarch of the Nogget household and the spectral co-host of the instructional carpentry segment How To with Jeb. His soul is perpetually bound within a single upright rectangular plank of unfinished construction timber.
Overview & Persona
Appearing at the workshop bench alongside his son Jeb Nogget, Jeb’s Dad communicates as an animated, faint spectral sketch embedded directly into the wood grain. Despite having no lungs or vocal cords, he maintains an abrasive, cantankerous, and hyper-critical presence, providing biting commentary on workshop safety, joinery techniques, and his son’s perpetual life shortcomings.
He displays a profound, open disdain for Jeb’s woodworking skills and emotional intelligence, constantly comparing him unfavorably to his golden-child brother, Jet Nogget.
Key Attributes & Lore

Spiritual Timber Vessel: Manifests inside a standard 2x4 (or wider board) resting upright on the workbench. His face appears as a floating, etched illustration within the knots of the pine.
The Patricide Implication: It is heavily implied throughout the workshop broadcasts that Jeb himself murdered his father and ritually bound his restless soul into the timber to force him into co-hosting instructional cable-access television. However, neither Jeb nor the board has ever outright confirmed the criminal specifics on air.
Parental Favoritism (Jet vs. Jeb): Never misses an opportunity to sing the praises of Jeb’s brother, Jet Nogget. Whether recounting Jet’s superior financial earnings, athletic prowess, or legitimate trade certifications, he treats Jeb as an embarrassing second-choice offspring.
Workshop Safety Tyrant: Frequently heckles Jeb whenever power tools, routers, or table saws are activated, demanding eye protection while actively hoping Jeb cuts a finger off so he can point out improper form.

characters/jeff-ripple.title: Jeff Ripple
characters/jeff-ripple.content:
Jeff Ripple

Jeff Ripple (full name Jeff Ebenezer Ripple) is a studio newsreader, human-interest correspondent, and community liaison on Barely Informed News.
Stationed alongside the primary newsroom desk, Ripple monitors incoming viewer dispatches, delivers offbeat news bulletins, and provides sharp on-air commentary alongside lead anchor Case Blackwell.
Overview
Ripple serves as the network’s human-interest reporter and live audience conduit. He reads breaking viewer reactions to major headlines, tracks eccentric domestic stories, and frequently trades barbs with both Blackwell and high-velocity cultural correspondent Hype Train.
Despite positioning himself as a serious newsroom correspondent in the mold of a legacy Jon Stewart, Ripple’s journalistic ambitions are constantly derailed by chat trolling, technical difficulties, and his bitter professional obsessions.
The Bitter Rivalry with Ben Hooper
Ripple’s defining professional obsession is his bitter, one-sided rivalry with Ben Hooper.
Hooper is a real-life reporter (notably known for UPI’s Odd News wire) who covers corny, wholesome, and absurd human-interest topics—such as dog surfing competitions, runaway livestock, and quirky Guinness World Records—which reliably produce viral video hits. Hooper is not a character on Barely Informed News, has never appeared on the broadcast, and is almost certainly completely unaware that Barely Informed News even exists.
Nevertheless, Ripple harbors a deep, boiling hatred for Hooper. The Barely Informed News audience and live chat constantly fawn over Hooper’s corny reporting style and celebrate his antics specifically to infuriate Ripple. Whenever Blackwell plays a Ben Hooper UPI audio package on-air or chat floods the prompter with praise for Hooper’s stories, Ripple is driven to visible jealousy, alternately fuming at the audience’s lowbrow taste or sarcastically proclaiming through gritted teeth that he is “the number one Ben Hooper fan.”
Key Eras & Bits

The Catchphrase: In Episode 2026-06-29, Ripple demanded Case acknowledge “I’m Jeff Ripple” as his official network catchphrase. (The “Jam EFE” era and Steam Shirt No Pants album from later in that broadcast belong to Jevrything, whose name is routinely mistranscribed as “Jeff Everything.“)
The Monday Correspondent: Positioned himself as the network’s dedicated Monday desk anchor, occasionally missing shifts due to extended vet appointments for his cat.
The Middle Name: In Episode 2026-02-04, Ripple’s middle name was given as “Retain” (supposedly anglicized at Ellis Island from “Return”). In Episode 2026-11-10, while the desk enjoyed reading out Pete Hegseth’s full name, Case asked for Ripple’s and got “Jeff Ebenezer Ripple.” When Case balked, Ripple shut the matter down: “It’s too late, Case. That’s my middle name now… It’s too late because it’s always been.” Ebenezer is the current canon.
Weekend Odds and Ends: Anchors feature segments curating bizarre North American regional stories (e.g., British Columbia floating islands, Virginia bat encounters, and Tarzana wildlife brawls).

characters/jevrything.title: Jevrything
characters/jevrything.content:
Jevrything

Jevrything (currently; ask again tomorrow) is a self-proclaimed teen pop sensation, “generational talent,” and the network’s most surgically altered musician. He debuted as Jay Drilla and has since cycled through more names than anyone on Barely Informed News can keep track of — least of all lead anchor Case Blackwell.
Overview
Jevrything drops into the studio as a news co-anchor, Amongst the Web co-host, or Town Hall panelist, and immediately treats the broadcast as a promotional opportunity: every headline is a lead-in to a new single, every audience question is answered with an album plug. He wears a purple floral blazer, is constantly compared to Justin Bieber (he finds this rude), and insists he is “really young.”
He usually arrives trailed by a swarm of flies — “I still have the horde of flies that follow me about” — which Case refers to as his “Legion of Bugs.” Jevrything prefers to think of them as fans.
The Name
Jevrything’s signature bit is that his name is never the same twice, and Case is always saying it wrong.
Each appearance opens with the same ritual. Case greets him by whatever he was called last time; Jevrything corrects him with the name he is going by today, usually announced via a text from his manager, a consulting firm, or “what everybody’s saying.” The new name is typically a near-homophone of the old one, spelled in a way that cannot be derived from its pronunciation (“It’s actually just Jeznery right now.” / “How do you spell that?” / “You don’t.”). When Case finally says it correctly, the name has already changed.
The gag is compounded by a running confusion with the network’s actual Jeff, Jeff Ripple: “It’s really close to Jeff.” / “Yeah, and a plane is close to a jet.” For a while the fans “shortened it to Jeff,” and the speech-to-text archive of the show has been mistaking the two ever since.































































































EpisodeName(s)How it went2025-06-07Jay Drilla”That’s my stage name.” The J stands for Justin, but his manager said that was “a little too close to some other stuff.” Drilla is short for his real name, Drembeland, which he is not supposed to say.2025-06-26J. Drilla, “Vibe Killer,” “Skunk Master”Case has forgotten his name entirely and has to replay the debut clip to find it. “That’s a bad name.”2025-07-12Jay Driller → Drilla → Drillist → Jay → Drip → Jibdnin → Job Startup → JSUThe manager-text era begins: “My manager just texted me. It’s just Jay now.” “I had a great era as Jibdnin. Everybody loved Jibdnin, but you got to grow in this business.”2025-07-25Jay Everything → J.E.V. → “Jeff with a V""It’s short for Jeff everything. You just have to hear them.”2025-11-18Jeznery → Jesans → Jesnic → JevrythingChanged for the album promo tour; reverted on air when the tour ended. The new thing is to move your name around — the syllables in it.”2026-04-11SlangSpelled J-L-L-O-N-G, “with a Jello in there.” Calling him Jevrything is allowed, “but it’s rude.”2026-05-22Jimny-free / Jim Nephrim”Artists evolve.” Briefly changes his name and his answer to “Rush Hour” mid–Town Hall.2026-05-29Jefferything”Spelled differently than the way you said it… You’re never gonna get it.”2026-06-29Jam EFE”Obviously people know me as Jeff Everything, but right now I’m in my Jam EFE era.” Case: “Is that really an effective marketing technique?“2026-07-17Jevening”Yeah, you’re saying it right for once. Way to go.”2026-07-24The Jimmary ThingRiding the viral Jimothy the raccoon trend. Case: “You’ve changed it every time you’ve said it so far to me.”
Surgeries & Body Modifications
Jevrything’s other defining trait is an endless series of cosmetic procedures, almost always pitched as beauty or skin treatments, that leave him unable to do something basic. Chat reports he is nearly done with his “plastic surgery punch card” for a free sandwich, and that he “doesn’t have normal bones anymore.”

Song installation surgery on his thyroid, which “sort of limits my vocal range,” plus a second procedure so that he always sounds auto-tuned (2025-06). He cannot smile and must stretch his face daily so it doesn’t seize up.
Bug removed from his eye (2025-07-12).
30% snake throat, installed to improve his vocals; “by the end of the year large amounts of my tissue will be snake, on the inside only.” He is “one of the throat goats” (2025-09-13).
Face melting off the side mid-broadcast; “good thing I still look okay from the front” (2025-09-05).
Shark/snake gel treatment and bone excision to thin his bones “so that my skin is more lustrous.” Wears a hat “to keep my head in” so his scalp doesn’t slough off; grows back hair only when gorilla skin is grafted on to exfoliate (2025-11-18).
Holographic teeth made of light (“they don’t bite very good”), sand lips, “mellow eye” surgery (marshmallows painted like eyes, leaving him functionally blind), a deep-fryer skin treatment, and removal of his ability to look or sound sad — not a problem “if you do happy songs” (2026-02-06).
Paper-mâché jaw, restricting him to non-solids (he steals Chet’s shake); possibly a nose converted to a more “efficient” orifice (2026-03-27).
Road salt bone marrow (bones now ~30% salt, for clear skin), a 23andMe result of “100% bleach,” and vocal cords removed to fix his formerly deep voice (2026-04-01).
Surgeon “mechanisms” that periodically assemble around him to keep everything in order (2026-05-12).
Piano-wire vocal cords, which occasionally leave him unable to talk; asks whether he can “girth out” his cords (2026-05-29).
Custom whale-bone genitals — “really tidy down there,” going for “more symmetry than size” (2026-06-29).
Three years of cryotherapy in his 20s, for skin that is “nice and plump but hard”; skipped COVID entirely (2026-07-17).
A “diaphragm module” — the hole in him he calls his DMs, now his only way to eat (2026-07-24).

Music & Discography
Jevrything’s catalog is vast, heart-obsessed, and almost entirely unreleased. His release strategy has included flash drives sold in a Best Buy parking lot, a barcode in one bowling alley in Des Moines, prompts on Google Gemini, “Laud” (not Claude), singing in the background of strangers’ selfie videos, and hiding CDs in poultry (“You can’t put a hyperlink in a chicken, Case”). By mid-2026 “99% of my songs are actually now AI,” at a rate of roughly 3,000 songs a day.
Titles plugged on air include:

Singles: “Party Down,” “Two Becomes Heart,” “Break That Heart Wall Down,” “Youth” (his attempt to break into the Chinese pop market), “Small Town Kids,” “Every Day Is a Perfect 10” (sold to Walgreens), “Style’s Too Hot,” “Unique New York,” “Wave Scooter” (like surfing, but with a scooter), “Forever Not Adulting,” “Hungry Eyeball,” “Boring Is Just Another Word for Your Heartbreak,” “AJ Nothing but a Big Old Sack of DNA,” “I Like to Be Scared of the Things That Break.”
Albums: Two Time Pass (his third), Everything Is Everything (the title of three of his albums), two stealth country albums, the spoken-word Screaming into the Waterfall, Love That Make You Man, Steam Shirt No Pants (cover: his shirt is steam), 45 Months, 46 Months, and You’re Part of the Problem.
Features: the bridge of DJ C4’s mayonnaise parody “Mayo Slather” with Mancini Smooth (2025-08-02), and a verse on Hype Train’s clown track (2026-05-22).

His style shifts as often as his name: earnest teen pop, a “dark and twisted” phase, soft pop ballads, a 90s hip-hop detour, and repeated threats to “go conservative.”
Relationships

Case Blackwell: His long-suffering anchor, who cannot remember, pronounce, or spell any of his names and keeps reminding him that music is DJ C4’s job — “Our job here is the news.” Jevrything maintains that Case “just doesn’t understand art” and has “too many emotions.”
Marfus Darfus: A fellow vocalist Case cannot tell apart from him (“There’s one cent of difference between you”). Jevrything insists they “sound very different, actually,” and a Darfus–Jevrything collab has been promised.
Gianna Wettmichel: Fellow Town Hall panelist (2025-11-18) who enjoys that he gives back her guff and asks the panel to please stop plugging albums.
Everything Bagel and Jay Nothing: His Town Hall co-panelists of 2026-04-01 and 2026-05-22 respectively. Jevrything out-philosophizes the bagel, and considers the void-voiced Jay Nothing a beautiful collaborator.
Pepito: Approached about management (“Yo, Pepito, I’m open to changing management”).
Dr. Chath: Counseled him through the flies, his father, and loneliness in his debut Therapy session: “Embrace the flies.”

Notable Moments

The Debut (2025-06-07): After Guy Redacted “redacted” Case’s co-hosts, up-and-coming artist Jay Drilla fills in, speed-runs viewer headlines while plugging songs between them, then confesses to Dr. Chath that he lives on salt-and-vinegar Pringles and has always felt alone.
The Manager Texts (2025-07-12): A full news block punctuated by name changes arriving from his manager by text, culminating in “Job Startup,” spelled “J-O-B-S-T-A-R-T… to the P,” and its fan nickname JSU.
The Face Melt (2025-09-05): Midway through co-anchoring the news, his face begins melting off the side; he signs off with the improvised lyric “Jevs is Jevrything and Jevrything is all the news.”
The Promo Tour Finale (2025-11-18): Reveals the Town Hall is the last stop of his album tour, so his name is “back to everything.”
The Jam EFE Listening Party (2026-06-29): Hosts a listening party for Steam Shirt No Pants, changing outfits on camera between cuts, and claims the album already tops the Surfshark charts.
The Bathroom Wander (2026-07-17): Disappears mid-broadcast after Hype Train’s piss rap; Case frantically flips through his “rolodex” to get him back.

Open Questions

What is his actual name? Only “Drembeland” has ever slipped out.
Is the swarm of flies a fan base, a medical condition, or a side effect of one of the surgeries?
How much of his original body remains?
Will any of his music ever be released anywhere but a bowling alley in Des Moines?
Will the long-promised Marfus Darfus collab happen?

Jizzbo (occasionally misheard in archive notes as Jizbo or Gizbo) is a recurring Barely Informed News persona — wall electrician / maintenance dwarf, guest vocalist, and later a mock-trial witness who answers examination with a conga.
Overview & Persona
Jizzbo first appears during Join the Wall as the studio electrician who descends into the drywall with Munch, later returns as a DJ C4 guest artist, and is woven into Crum marital lore as “Freddie Jizzbo.” During the 2026-03-07 peen.ui IP mock trial he is called back from the mountain, announces “I’m here. It’s me. It’s jizzbo,” claims to still be in great shape, and meets a defense prompt by launching into Gloria Estefan’s “Conga” instead of testimony.
The court sustains the musical interruption despite Jizzbo clarifying he does not believe a question was asked.

characters/johnny-dick-big.title: Johnny Dick Big
characters/johnny-dick-big.content:
Johnny Dick Big

Johnny Dick Big is a self-described porn expert who appeared via portable green screen on Barely Informed News, defending communal comment culture as the lost art of erotic magazine letter columns.
Overview & Persona
Booked into a late Conspiracy Desk slot on 2026-10-19 after Pepito supposedly “got the porn guy,” Johnny materializes against a poorly keyed cityscape backdrop — towering pompadour, cartoon-thick eyebrows, loud blue patterned blazer. He insists the name is an homage to favorite stars — “I am a porn expert I’m not a porn performer” — and carries a green screen everywhere in case he needs to be whisked to a set.
His thesis: leaving comments on porn is cool because theaters used to be community events, magazine letter columns used to be a subscribed correspondence culture, and modern viewers who only tip OnlyFans without writing are abandoning the art form. Case pushes back on encouraging parasocial obsession with people one masturbates to; Johnny asks who the expert is, declares himself in demand, and negotiates a $250 payment before vanishing.
Signature bits

Portable green screen (improperly keyed) for anywhere-set readiness
“I’m a fucking porn expert” / “Who’s the expert here?” refrains
Magazine letter-column nostalgia as the moral case for porn comments
Abrupt exit with a $250 ask

Appearances

characters/kendelle.title: Kendelle
characters/kendelle.content:
Kendelle

Kendelle is lead anchor Case Blackwell’s real-life and in-show girlfriend, making occasional in-studio appearances across Barely Informed News.
Overview
Unlike the studio’s remote correspondents or desk analysts, Kendelle appears whenever she walks through the “studio” (Blackwell’s home streaming room). Her entrances are instantly recognized by viewers thanks to her own dedicated signature theme music that Blackwell cues whenever she walks across the frame.
In addition to spontaneous on-camera walk-throughs, Kendelle is a freelance video editor, Blackwell’s cooperative gaming partner (regularly playing games like BigWog and Friend Slap), and his co-host for joint podcast and self-improvement projects (such as their “looks maxing” experiments).
Blackwell frequently shares personal life updates involving Kendelle—including hiding engagement rings while preparing for “husband money”, surviving 15-hour emergency flight layovers in Denver, and navigating health insurance coverage lapses.

characters/liliana.content:
Liliana Breathinschmit

Liliana Breathinschmit (known on air simply as Liliana) is a recurring in-studio contributor and news desk co-anchor on Barely Informed News. Her on-screen tagline: “World Affairs & Kinks.”
Overview
Liliana serves as an irreverent, sharp-witted desk partner opposite lead anchor Case Blackwell. Known for her direct, dry banter, she frequently punctures Case’s journalistic pretensions, scrutinizes studio staffing decisions, and assists in breaking down international wire copy.
The Year-Long “Vacation” & Return
Liliana was absent from Barely Informed News for approximately a full year before making a surprise return to the desk on the August 14, 2026 broadcast.

The Vacation Claim: Liliana framed her prolonged absence as an extended, self-granted “vacation” or sabbatical. Upon returning, she playfully insisted that Case had called her pleading for her return because he was “helpless without you.” She presented a slideshow of travel photos directly on the broadcast feed and repeatedly demanded retroactive paid time off (PTO) for her entire year away.
Control-Room Mix-Up: Network lore later held that her lengthy desk absence coincided with a period when Case had misplaced critical studio tracking equipment required for her on-air appearance; once the kit was recovered and calibrated, she was promptly restored to the newsroom desk.

Broadcast Role & Dynamic

Desk Co-Anchor: Sits alongside Case during the main News block, co-reading headlines from Reuters and the Associated Press.
Studio Gossip & Banter: Keeps tabs on internal newsroom politics, noting missing staffers (such as Sammy and Tyler), teasing Case about his experimental haircuts during her time away, and monitoring chat reactions.
Hype Train Dispatcher: Frequently reads out incoming subscription alerts and network milestones from the studio monitors.

characters/marfus-darfus.content:
Marfus Darfus

Marfus Darfus (frequently introduced as Marfis Darfus) is a guest host and recurring contributor on Barely Informed News, best known for helming the network’s viewer viral clip review desk, Amongst the Web.
Overview
Marfus Darfus is an eccentric on-air personality whose casual demeanor and unvarnished honesty make him an immediate network favorite. Introduced on the broadcast with his signature greeting, “Hey, it’s me, it’s Marfis Darfus!”, he brings an earnest, slightly bewildered sensibility to reviewing internet culture.
Lead anchor Case Blackwell and in-studio contributor Liliana frequently express relief when Marfus takes over the desk, openly stating that having Marfus on air is infinitely preferable to enduring Munch’s volatile rants.
Personality & Mannerisms

Signature Catchphrase: Opens segments with an enthusiastic declaration of identity: “Hey, it’s me, it’s Marfis Darfus!”
Asexual Philosophy: Marfus candidly reveals during broadcasts that he does not partake in romantic or sexual endeavors, stating plainly: “I don’t actually do sex… I don’t believe in it.” When a pause settles over the desk, he notes that despite the “pregnant pause,” he himself “cannot get pregnant.”
Idiosyncratic Decimal Rating Scale: When evaluating viewer submissions, Marfus employs surprisingly specific decimal scoring rather than round numbers (awarding a 6.44 to a dramatic Family Matters scene and a 5.5 to Love Island).
Philosophical Asides: Prone to existential commentary while watching surveillance or public footage. Upon witnessing a bewildered commuter riding an airport escalator, Marfus deduced the subject was navigating a profound “fugu state” (fugue state) where “it’s really about the journey… he discovered something we’ll never understand.”
Impatience with Stillness: Marfus prefers fast-paced, direct action, occasionally urging slow-paced viral submissions to move along, prompting Case to caution: “Marvis, don’t be rude.”

characters/munch.title: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters/munch.content:
Munch (Ralph Munchcut)

Ralph Munchcut (known on air simply as Munch) is a senior debate analyst on Barely Informed News, anchoring the network’s premier political debate clash, Munch & Crum.
Overview
Munch serves as the combative, unapologetic political counterweight to Crum on Barely Informed News. Distinguished by his disheveled silver mane, Munch brings relentless swagger and hostility to the debate desk.
On 2024-05-15, Crum’s first debate-score victory after 200+ losses broke Munch into the soft alter ego Al Manchester (debuted as Ale Chrome Chester / Ale Munchester). The nice-guy shell lasted through early June; by mid-June Munch was restored (hair back, ego intact), with Crum insisting Al remains trapped inside.
Their volatile dynamic also forms the backbone of the Crum Punch trilogy: Munch goaded the 2025 face-punch Crumsplosion, then rescued Crum from hell after weeks of volleyball-corpse denial, and finally agitated for the 2026 groin-punch sequel. On September 7, 2026, the punch backfired: Crum went “demon mode” in his hell form, and the fireball burned Munch down to an immortal talking skeleton (see Skeleton Munch).
Skeleton Munch
Since 2026-09-07, Munch has been a living, talking skeleton. It’s a new manifestation of Munch himself, not an alter ego and not Al Manchester.

Origin. When the Rock-afire Gorilla finally threw the long-awaited Crum Dick Punch, the stage erupted in “a shit load of fire” [1:50:40]. Munch, standing by to gloat, took the blast; Crum walked away unscathed. Munch’s verdict: “You went all fucking demon mode” [1:51:55]. “You turn me into a skeleton?” he demands; Crum calls that “a little bit of an exaggeration… there was an accident” [1:56:24].
Crum’s defense. Crum calls it Munch’s “incredibly self-imposed condition” and says “even in my hell form my intention was [not] for you to become a talking skeleton,” blaming Munch for “absorbing a fireball” (2026-11-03 [54:25–54:51]). Munch: “you still tried to make me one.”
Embracing it. Munch insists he “meant to be a skeleton,” that it shows off his superior bone structure, and that “skeletons are so in right now.” He calls himself a “skelly,” bills himself Skellomunch (2026-10-22), and claims the title Lord of the Dead with a summonable penis (2026-09-25). He bristles at assumptions about his “skeletal identity” (2026-10-19).
Green level-up. During the Rebuild Rennerton Valheim stream he turns green after combat (2026-10-23), later explaining he “leveled up” by killing a spirit to progress his tech tree (2026-10-26).
Status. Permanent so far: he debates, mayors Rennerton, and haunts the desk as a skeleton.

Canon notes

Since 2026-09-07 Munch is a permanent talking skeleton (“Skeleton Munch”, “Skellomunch”, “skelly”), burned down by Crum’s demon/hell-form fireball when the Crum Dick Punch backfired. Tag skeleton beats to Crum Dick Punch or Munch, never to Al Manchester.
Al Manchester is only the bald, soft-spoken alter ego from the 2024-05-15 scoreboard breakdown (concluded June 2024). Skeleton Munch is not Al Manchester.

characters/pepito.title: Pepito
characters/pepito.content:
Pepito

Pepito is the Executive Producer of Barely Informed News.
Appearing from the control room via the dedicated “Producer Cam,” Pepito is a canine broadcast executive featuring pointed ears, alert dark eyes, and a distinguished tuft of white hair. He is also occasionally designated on station monitors as Peptron 3000.
Overview & Network Operations
Pepito oversees control room operations, production switching, and broadcast timing. He was promoted to Executive Producer following the unceremonious firing of former producer Peter Gibbon.
Pepito officially opens every broadcast at the top of the hour with his signature station announcement:

“I’m Pepito, I’m the dog that produces the show, and now it is live, and I’m a dog.”

Beyond station management, Pepito is known for asserting his demands across the control room intercom, which have included refusing to perform parlor tricks and declaring his intent to consume an entire bag of sangria over holiday weekends.
Key Attributes & Lore

Executive Authority: Coordinates live production queues, switching feeds, and managing anchor handoffs.
Station Cold-Open: Delivers the official top-of-hour broadcast sign-on and countdown across all network channels.
Audio Recognition: Demonstrates an acute ear for live audio discrepancies, famously identifying vocal imposters during metaphysical control room incidents.
Beverage & Culinary Demands: Known for issuing sudden hospitality demands to newsroom interns, notably requiring large quantities of pasta and wine.
