characters/peter-gibbon.title: Peter Gibbon
characters/peter-gibbon.content:
Peter Gibbon

Peter Gibbon (formally credited on air as Peter G.) is the disgraced former executive producer of Barely Informed News, currently designated on screen as the network’s “News Stowaway & Food Eater.”
Distinctive for his stout frame, round spectacles, nasal delivery, and prominent cleft chin, Gibbon is widely regarded as one of the most abrasive and reviled figures to ever step foot in the studio.
Overview
Gibbon served as the original producer of Barely Informed News before being terminated and stripped of his security credentials due to gross managerial incompetence, leading directly to the hiring of Pepito.
Following his dismissal, Gibbon refused to vacate the network facilities. Evading building security, he took up permanent residence inside the structural crawlspaces and drywall of the newsroom. From these interior wall cavities, Gibbon regularly sneaks into the broadcast booth, raids the staff refrigerator, commandeers unattended broadcast feeds, and interrupts live telecasts to the immense fury of lead anchor Case Blackwell.
Key Attributes & Lore

Structural Wall Inhabitant: Squats full-time within the studio drywall, navigating behind control room consoles and emerging through crawlspace access panels.
On-Screen Lower Third: Billed on broadcast graphics as “Peter G. NEWS STOWAWAY & FOOD EATER”.
Staff Contempt: Universally despised by anchors, technical crew, and viewers alike, who groan whenever his voice filters through the air ducts.
Physical Feats & Delusions: Boasts of deadlifting beer kegs, claims dubious former military intelligence connections, and harbors an obsession with model rocketry.

Rick is a veteran field correspondent and tactical media analyst on Barely Informed News, serving as anchor of the network’s viral media evaluation desk, Amongst the Web.
Characterized by a weathered, stern expression and military-grade discipline, Rick brings uncompromising tactical scrutiny to viral internet oddities and viewer-submitted video files.

Drawing upon an extensive operational background, Rick evaluates absurd modern internet culture through the lens of strategic threat assessment and surveillance, reviewing user submissions while monitoring audience sentiment scores.

characters/rob-alvey.title: Rob Alvey
characters/rob-alvey.content:
Rob Alvey

Rob Alvey is a ban-happy theme-park and roller-coaster obsessive who has been showing up on Barely Informed News since 2023. He wanders into segments to ban, block, and “cancel” whoever is in front of him, and his favorite target is Trip on Trip on the Street. His surname is rendered inconsistently in transcripts (Elvie, Alvy, Alvie), but the canonical spelling is Alvey.
Overview & Persona
Rob is a grumpy, thin-skinned gatekeeper who treats every room he enters as his own park to police. His reflex answer to any slight is to ban the person responsible, often from places he has no authority over (Cedar Point, Orlando, the studio itself). He usually gets banned right back by Case, Trip, or both. Each return is pitched as a fresh start, and each one collapses within minutes.
He looks different every time he appears and takes it personally when anyone says so (“It’s insulting that everybody keeps telling me and only me that I look different”).
On air, his name has turned into a verb for indiscriminate banning: during the 2026-11-10 news block Case argued “you can’t just Rob Alvey everything,” then admitted “Rob does.”
Signature Bits

The ban hammer: Bans chat, guests, hosts, and entire theme parks’ worth of visitors on sight. When Case and another guest both try to reason with him in 2025-10-13, he answers, “You are both banned.”
Harassing Trip on the Street: Rob is a near-permanent fixture among Trip’s park interviewees. He bans Trip and the park crowd, steals the mailed invitation to Trip’s son Chase’s wedding and blocks Trip’s number (2024-06-26, where Trip finally microphone-punches him), poses as a fake cop with tape (2025-04-04), bans Case from Orlando (2025-03-07), and keeps trying to negotiate his own unban (2024-07-25). Trip is eventually authorized to “blow his ass away” on sight (2025-06-13).
Theme parks & roller coasters: Everything comes back to coasters. He bans everyone from Cedar Point (2024-05-15), explains the “rollercoaster intestines” theory (2024-06-05), and got re-banned in 2025-06-13 over a roller-coaster game endorsement dispute.
Alvalstonia: In 2023-12-02, chat demanded his return and he claimed citizenship of the fictional nation of Alvalstonia, “where roller coasters loop,” with an anthem that turned out to be a war dirge for “the day all Alvalstonians got booted out of Six Flags Illinois.” He called his banning xenophobia, was banned anyway, and his voice distorted into Rick on the way out.
Failed reform arcs: He has returned claiming to have turned over a new leaf at least twice (2025-09-10, 2025-06-13) and reverted to banning both times.

Relationships

Trip: His main target and nemesis. Rob haunts Trip’s bushes, bans the park, and sabotaged his son’s wedding.
Robbie Love: Rival and frequent mix-up. Robbie is the roller-skates guy and Rob is the coasters guy. They argued over whose name was whose on a joint call-in (2025-10-13) and traded verses in a DJ C4 diss track (2025-10-18).
Case: Checks in with Rob only under chat pressure and “takes no pleasure in it.” Case usually ends the visit by banning him.
Mancini Smooth: Co-hosted a Town Hall with him in 2025-09-26 and mocked him throughout.

Sammy Seven Elbows

Sammy Seven Elbows (often shortened on air to Sammy; briefly billed as Sammy Six Elbows on debut) is a recurring correspondent and guest personality on Barely Informed News.
Overview
Sammy debuted as a surprise guest commentator during Biden press-conference coverage, was quickly renamed from Six Elbows to Seven Elbows, and settled into a recurring desk presence—sometimes as a conspiracy correspondent, sometimes as a casual in-studio contributor billed simply as Sammy. Chat and staff treat the short name and the full elbow count as the same person.
In later lore, the sock puppet Hate Sock outs himself as Sammy Seven Elbows in sock form—former president, now fabric.

Night Man / Biden haunt — Claims President Biden resembles the “Night Man” who haunted his bedside since childhood.
Epstein cloning desk — Early correspondent run covering Daily Mail cloning allegations on the same telecast that later birthed Munch’s Al Manchester alter ego.
The Thing Song — Flash-poll win triggers an AI Cisco “Thong Song” parody about an illegal pickle-cart past and Italian swag.

characters/scrum.title: Scrum
characters/scrum.content:
Scrum

Scrum (occasionally Eugene Scrum; chat-styled Scrumfuscious; high-school nickname Blood Dog) is the on-air alter ego / temp-hire persona of debate analyst Leonard Crum on Barely Informed News — same bald pate and blazer energy, billed as a separate man when Crum is “out,” punished, or moonlighting off the debate desk.
Overview
Scrum debuts in mid-December 2023 as a one-day temp Munch installs to needle Crum, then sticks around via a year-long contract Case claims to have signed on the spot. He later resurfaces as Crum’s news-desk and web-desk alias — reading wire copy under protest, co-hosting Amongst the Web, fulfilling contractual rap marathons, and insisting he is a mononym: “Scrum, period.”
Visually he reads as Crum’s twin (bald, bearded, blazer) rather than a costume change; the name and billing do the split. Chat treats cousin-logic and “Scrumfuscious” middle-name jokes as ongoing lore. On 2026-11-24 he disclosed that classmates called him Blood Dog (“dog spelled like the classic animal”), after chat floated “Big Natural.”
Signature bits

Temp hire / Scrum vs Crum — Munch champions Scrum as the superior desk partner; chat polls pit Scrum against Crum.
Eugene Scrum quit bit — Early dodge where Crum claims to have quit and reappears under the Eugene Scrum name to avoid debating Munch.
“Scrum, period” — Mononym identity with no middle or last name.
Blood Dog — High-school nickname he refuses to explain beyond “you had to be there.”
Contractual obligations — Monthly appearances, 30-minute rap sessions, news rundowns read under protest (“words are pointless”).
News / web desk fill-in — Wire-reading, Amongst the Web guest seat, crypto-summit mockery while billed as Scrum.

characters/ten.title: Ten
characters/ten.content:
Ten

Ten is Trent’s cousin. He arrived unannounced on the At the Movies set in 2026-11-10 while Trent was “showing him what I do.” He wears the same black beanie and beard as Trent, and Case noted, “He looks exactly like you.”
Overview & Persona
Everybody calls him Ten, but “his real name is Six.” He is sixteen (“Convenient age. It’s got a six in it”), and he rates every trailer a six “because I am six.”
Ten is extremely sensitive to vibes. Any confusion about his name, any shushing, any slight from chat ruins his entire day. His coping strategy is to leave and kick a tree “until either my foot broke or the tree… First one to break breaks.” Ten has never won against a tree.
He insists on respect from everyone, including his cousin: “Don’t shush me, young blood. Respect.” He has also explained that “shwish” is the respectful way to say “shush.”
Debut
Ten’s first visit to At the Movies played out in this order:

Nobody could work out whether he was saying “Ten” or “ten,” and he tried to leave because “everybody’s not being chill.”
Chat won him back with the nickname “Battle Arena Toshin Ten”: “That does rock. I’m back in… I felt like maybe I was at my lowest ever.”
A chat insult re-ruined his day, so he went out to kick the tree, despite pleas of “Ten, don’t let the darkness come for you, man” and “Ten, don’t do it, dude. You’re gonna break your foot again.”
He rated Long Haired Businessmen a six (“It’s a serious rating. Not everything’s fucking funny, man”).
Mid-trailer he announced, “I broke my foot… I’m gonna have to talk to my fucking aunt about this.”
A few trailers later he broke his other foot as well, kicking the tree from a handstand (“That is impressive upper body strength, but Ten, it’s a misuse of it”).
He left in Ten’s Chariot, a wheelchair kept chained to the back of an electric bike “just in case he breaks his feet, both of them, kicking trees.”

Relationships

Trent: Cousin and lookalike. Trent brought him to work to show him the job.
Chris: Trent’s parole officer, who was on set for Ten’s debut.

Appearances

“I always rate things six. My nickname’s Ten, but I’ll rate it a six, because I am six.” (2026-11-10)

characters/tommy-biglaw.content:
Tommy Biglaw

Tommy Biglaw (also billed as Little Tommy Big Law, Lil Tommy Big Law, or Little Tommy Biglaw) is the high-priced legal counsel representing lead anchor Case Blackwell and Barely Informed News.
Distinguished by the facial features and lisping cadence of an infant paired with a dark, impeccably groomed full beard, Biglaw is treated across the network as a licensed, high-billing attorney despite his youth.
Overview
Tommy first appears in the archive as toddler attorney Little Tommy Big Law, delivering surreal legal takes (Trump conviction snacks-and-jail analysis, nipple jurisprudence on Drake’s UMG suit). Later billing shortens to Tommy Biglaw, but the infant face, baby-talk lisp, and predatory fee schedule stay continuous.
On the 2026-08-26 broadcast, he was summoned after viewers threatened legal action over unhinged video material Blackwell aired. Despite the lisp (“16 was” instead of laws), he bills strictly by the minute ($2,500 per infraction), then turns on his own client as alter-ego “Big Tommy Prosecutor,” demanding a $40,000 settlement before attempting to seize studio milk.

Trent is a self-styled cultural taste-maker of deliberately ambiguous age — framed as a truant teen doing court-ordered community service on air. He broadcasts from a green-screen movie theater in a beanie-and-blazer look, screens trailers, and lectures Case about green-screen actor safety, franchise fatigue, and whatever Chat just yelled.

characters/trip-bradstein.content:
Trip Bradstein

Trip Bradstein is an eccentric field correspondent for Barely Informed News.
Residing permanently in the bushes of a public park, Bradstein is the network’s dedicated “man on the street” reporter, conducting remote interview dispatches for his signature segment, Trip on the Street.
Overview
Unlike the studio-bound newsroom staff, Bradstein lives on location within public park shrubbery, periodically emerging from multi-month “bush hibernations” when called upon to deliver dispatches. During his broadcasts, Bradstein intercepts passing park visitors to collect their unfiltered “on the street” opinions on questions and discussion topics sourced directly from audience submissions.
Bradstein is fiercely protective of his outdoor beat, regularly proclaiming “I’ll never leave these streets!” despite the hazards and surreal encounters of park life. His live interviews feature an unpredictable parade of park denizens, impromptu interruptions by fellow network personalities (such as Hype Train), and confused pedestrians—including Bradstein’s own mother, whom he failed to recognize, treating her on air as a random stranger.

characters/tub.title: Tub
characters/tub.content:
Tub

Tub is the dumbass who defended against 30 dumbasses in the 2026-10-26 edition of Encircled. He took the chair with the claim “No Uh,” outlasted every challenger chat threw at him, and walked out the winner without ending the segment properly.
Overview & Persona
Tub has glasses, a full beard, swollen lips, and a brown camo-print blazer. In his words, he is “wearing my brown red,” and “red brown don’t fuck around.” He opens by introducing himself several times (“my name’s tub”) and issuing vague threats to anyone who tries to mess with him, while openly admitting he doesn’t know where he is or what the segment is about.
He argues entirely by insult, counter-insult, and confident non sequitur. Despite that, or maybe because of it, he becomes an instant chat favorite.
Lore & Signature Bits

“No Uh”: Tub’s on-screen claim for the whole debate. Every counter claim is measured against it.
The brown red: His outfit color is a status signal. Wearing the brown red “means I’m not fucking around.”
Seven kids: He says he has “six kids… seven kids,” confirms it’s seven on his way out, and mentions a strained relationship with their mother. When an opponent suggests condoms, he claims he literally always wears one, including right now.
The 482: His cousin hand-makes “DumBuhs” sneakers from repurposed Reeboks. You have to be from the 482 to get a pair, and the cousin doesn’t ship.
Tacorita: A margarita with tacos in it, a staple of the quinceañera and birthday party circuit. Tub feels sorry for anyone who has never had one.
Grandpa’s advice: One challenger concedes, “I’m only a dumbass because my grandpa told me not to be a smartass and I took it to heart.” Tub admits it’s “fucking funny.”
Button trouble: Tub leaves to go get tacoritas for his kids and doesn’t hit the end-segment button, so Case has to end it himself.

Relationships

Case Blackwell: Off-panel, Case asks if he can “bring him back and give him more time” mid-debate. Afterwards he says “God damn it, Tub” about the broken exit and “I like that Tub guy.”
Chat: Immediately campaigns “Tub for new correspondent.” Case agrees that “Tub sounds like he could run for state senate.”

Appearances

Notable Quotes

“My name’s Tub. I’m wearing my brown red.”
“If anybody’s trying to fuck with me, maybe think again, dude.”
“Red brown don’t fuck around.”
“You have to be from the 482 to have those, and I ain’t ever seen you before.”
“I do have seven kids. Oh, I’m Tub. I have to go.”
Case: “It’s dangerous to let a tub into your studio.”

Notable Moments

Open Questions

Will chat get its wish and see Tub return as a correspondent, or as a candidate for state senate?
What is the 482, and is it anywhere near Rennerton?
Is “Tub” a first name, a last name, or a description?

BIN Lore is an unofficial community project created and maintained entirely by fans. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or associated in any official capacity with:

Case Blackwell

All character names, segment titles, slogans, broadcast graphics, audio excerpts, screencaps, and related media assets documented on this site are the intellectual property of their respective copyright holders, primarily Case Blackwell.
Their use on this wiki is conducted strictly under the Fair Use doctrine of United States copyright law (17 U.S.C. § 107), specifically for purposes of:

Short highlight clips linked from episode and character pages are cut by BIN Lore and posted to its fan channels on YouTube and TikTok (@binlore.wiki). These channels are unofficial and not monetized, and every clip is labeled as a fan clip.

Content across BIN Lore is written as if Barely Informed News were an authentic, high-stakes global news network. They are not intended as statements of fact regarding real individuals or organizations.

5. Takedown & Contact Policy
If you are a copyright holder or authorized representative (including Case Blackwell or his production team) and have questions, concerns, or requests regarding the archival material or screencaps hosted on this site, please submit an issue or pull request via the GitHub repository. Overview
On this historic Season 3 finale of Barely Informed News, lead anchor Case Blackwell hosts the final broadcast before departing for an extended two-week international leave in Thailand, culminating in the long-awaited climax to the Crum Dick Punch storyline. The telecast begins with executive producer Pepito setting up Labor Day expectations, followed by a news rundown covering the Lanterns series trailer posted by the White House, Trump’s Confederate memorial policy reversals, Trump’s defense of power-hungry AI data centers (‘have fun being poor’), the GPT-6 ‘Astro’ model autonomously speedrunning Portal, RFK Jr.’s cooking show, Ben Hooper’s UPI reports on a runaway floating island in BC and a deer stuck in a bathroom, and an archival Pros vs. Joes clip of a 13-year-old female orangutan overpowering a 363-pound champion sumo wrestler. Hype Train interrupts with a synthwave rant about the perfection of jeans and raps about girls wearing denim, before turning to subs. Gaming correspondent Brandon (CryptoZeu$) takes the remote desk for Intelligent Qube on PS1 via keyboard while fielding sponsor dispatches for Gooters’ $59.99 soggy cola-dipped chicken skins. The broadcast reaches its dramatic climax during Munch & Crum’s debate over ‘Any Last Words?’—where Crum insists his rigorous physical conditioning with weighted logs and steel underwear will withstand the blow. As the pneumatic Rock-afire Gorilla fires the fateful punch, a cataclysmic mechanical misfire erupts into an inferno, completely vaporizing the gorilla into dust and incinerating senior debate analyst Ralph Munchcut down to a living, talking skeleton. Undeterred, the skeletal Munch embraces his bone structure, argues for Crayola over RoseArt, and demands future debates as the network signs off.

Characters

Quick Lil Newsgiving for the FREAKS (2026-11-26)

Broadcast Date: 2026-11-26
Twitch VOD: Quick Lil Newsgiving for the FREAKS (ID: 2941854260)
Approx length: 1:55:43
Ingest run: tools/runs/2941854260/

Overview
Barely Informed News aired a shortened Thanksgiving telecast anchored by Case Blackwell, whose Twitch bot failed and left him tallying the 13 Freak Street Kickstarter by hand between headlines. The desk covered the president’s holiday Truth Social address, the wind-canceled Macy’s parade, a retired Citrus County drug dealer and the Hoop God’s UPI minute, after which Munch and Crum deadlocked over the second-best tragedy and whether Crum’s hell powers grounded the parade. Liliana and Trip Bradstein handled the closing submissions, and Executive Producer Pepito delivered a Thanksgiving rap that declined to thank anyone.
Segment rundown



































































































































StartEndSegmentNotes0:089:00News: Cold Open: Pepito’s Holiday Sign-OnExecutive Producer Pepito opens the holiday broadcast as the producing dog; the top-of-hour countdown rolls in with stray studio clapping and reversed control-room graphics that Case has to fix live.9:0012:45Banter: Holiday Housekeeping: No Breaks November and the Dead BotWith the Twitch bot down, Case tallies the 13 Freak Street Kickstarter by hand at $13,300, sets a $45 Thanksgiving-miracle goal, promises a Pepito Thanksgiving song, and announces a shortened holiday rundown.12:4516:34Banter: Anchor Warm-Up: Black Hole Hands and Vocal ExercisesCase takes the desk on a holiday, claims his hands were cursed by a black hole he tackled mid-field, and runs vocal exercises on air while chat pitches an anime-voice career.16:3427:21News: News: Trump’s Thanksgiving Truth Social AddressCase reads the Reuters setup on the president’s holiday post, then delivers the full Truth Social message down the barrel — patriots, ‘fake economic numbers,’ Sharia courts, Somalis, the White House ballroom, and a closing address to deported migrants.27:2131:34News: Wire: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade CancellationCase reads the official cancellation statement — 30-40 mph sustained winds, 60-65 mph gusts, coastal flood warning — and pitches a ‘doom parade’ of exploding floats through Manhattan while chat demands the Crum sabotage debate.31:3436:20Banter: Holiday Logistics: GTA 6, Pepito’s Song and Sunday TravelCase and Chet trade Grand Theft Auto notes, the Kickstarter crosses the threshold that obligates Pepito’s song, the parade moves to Saturday, and Case flags Sunday travel that leaves Monday and Tuesday streams unsettled.36:2041:19Banter: Hunting the Endgame Premiere Audience TapeCase recounts attending the first Avengers: Endgame screening at the Chinese Theatre and hunts YouTube for the audience-reaction recording he appears on, failing to locate it and closing the lore.41:1944:47Banter: Incentive Board: $14,000 and the Hoseue PodcastCase and Kendelle weigh milestone incentives — a three-hour Hoseue podcast at $14,000, new emotes contingent on Matt Liddell donating again, GTA VI at $20,000 — plus Friday’s cooking stream with Kendall’s friend Kat.44:4747:36Banter: YouTube Search: The AI Thanksgiving Day ParadeCase searches for the canceled parade stream, finds a synthetic parade video that YouTube has flagged as AI, and reads the comment section before returning to the rundown.47:3650:25News: Chat News: The Retired Drug Dealer of Citrus CountyAfter a detour through Allen County’s revived drug tip line, Case covers Angela Moore, 54, charged with intent to distribute after a lane-change stop produced a cut straw, a digital scale, 150 baggies and a handwritten ledger.50:2552:18News: Wire: Turkeys Run Down a Newton WalkerCase runs ABC7’s three-and-a-half-minute package on a woman chased by aggressive turkeys into a stranger’s car, complains about the runtime, and pushes ahead to the Hoop God.52:1858:35News: The Hoop God’s UPI All-News MinuteCase runs Ben Hooper’s Tuesday UPI minute — an Amazon MK-30 drone that clipped a fiber optic cable and crashed onto a neighbor’s garage, and the Newton turkey rescue — noting the Hoop God covered the turkey story in a fraction of ABC7’s time, then signs the Hoop Troupe comment.58:351:00:07News: Entertainment Wire: Al Roker’s GaspWith no parade to cover, Case substitutes the Al Roker and John Stamos penis-comment clip, grades the headline as sub-Hoop God quality, and pivots to chat comments.1:00:071:03:20Banter: Chat Comments and the Martha Stewart ScreamCase reads comments on the $20,000 GTA VI incentive and the Hoseue podcast, then the Martha Stewart and Craig Melvin clip sends Chet into a jealousy spiral over his girlfriend’s whereabouts.1:03:201:10:31Munch & Crum: Munch & Crum: The Second Best TragedyMunch refuses to rank himself against Crum’s bracket of tragedies, argues first place could be anything, and takes the win when his name lands on the prediction; Crum calls the pairing impossible and rejects the vote outright.1:10:311:16:18Munch & Crum: Munch & Crum: The Parade Sabotage ChargeCrum denies using hell powers to ground the Macy’s parade; Munch blames Crum’s uncontrolled weather and general effect on the ecosystem, disowns his own role in the resurrection to ‘Flesh Munch,’ and pledges further executions while Crum’s sneezing fit wrecks his throat.1:16:181:19:27Banter: Sign-Off Chatter: Freak Street and Heart ConditionsMunch warns chat that voting for Crum will explode their hearts while Crum confirms he never left 13 Freak Street; control-room glitches and stray feeds interrupt the close before Case hands to Liliana.1:19:271:29:59Amongst the Web: Amongst the Web: Holiday SubmissionsLiliana joins the desk to grade Case’s sexiness, then the pair run chat submissions from cream.team — a fake Scottish accent traced to North Park, New Jersey, a live Rick Astley sing, and the classic parade clip of a mascot balloon stomped out of existence.1:29:591:48:29Trip on the Street: Trip on the Street: Thanksgiving OpinionsTrip Bradstein works the park bushes through an incoming raid, an Aaron Rodgers opinion, Gundam versus Lego, a deviled-egg accusation, Wishbone with a knife, a floppy nutcracker stickup, Daddy Darfus on the meaning of life, and a Black Friday shopper, while the !trip submission system fails.1:48:291:55:43News: Sign-Off: Pepito’s Thanksgiving Song and the Freak Street RaidPepito is called in to collect the unlocked Thanksgiving song, refuses to thank chat, and Case closes the holiday telecast with a freak street raid and a promise of Friday’s cooking stream.
Characters

Pepito (speaking) — Executive producer who delivered the holiday cold open and later honored the Kickstarter threshold with a Thanksgiving rap that refused to thank chat.
Case (speaking) — Anchored a shortened Thanksgiving rundown alone, hand-tallied the Kickstarter after his bot failed, and handed the desk to Munch, Crum, Liliana and Trip.
Munch (speaking) — Skeleton debate analyst who claimed second best on a name-check vote and pinned Crum’s resurrection on an alternate ‘Flesh Munch.’
Crum (speaking) — Denied grounding the Macy’s parade with hell powers and spent the segment’s back half destroying his own throat sneezing.
Liliana (speaking) — Joined Case at the desk to grade his sexiness and co-run the chat-submitted Amongst the Web reels.
Trip (speaking) — Closed the broadcast from the park bushes with Thanksgiving opinions while his submission queue collapsed.
Kendelle (speaking) — Dropped by the studio to weigh $14,000 incentive options and the Arizona travel schedule before drifting out of frame.

Storyline updates

No Breaks November [9:23]: [09:23] The Thanksgiving telecast is logged toward the month-long No Breaks November commitment, with the parade watch pushed to Saturday and a cooking stream added for Friday.
Crum Dick Punch [1:13:54]: [1:13:54] Munch makes ‘die infinitely’ a campaign promise, pledging to run for president so Crum’s executions can continue past the punch that already landed.

Lore notes

[0:33:21] Case states he has already brought the retired AI Rooney desk back, and treats a second revival as an available Kickstarter incentive.
[0:56:26] Case formalizes the network’s Hoop Troupe fandom, signing comments on the Hoop God’s UPI minute ‘Hoop Troupe. Out.’
[1:11:55] Munch: Munch disclaims Crum’s return from hell, attributing the resurrection to an alternate version of himself he names Flesh Munch.
[1:13:54] Munch: Munch adds a presidential run to his anti-Crum platform, promising to make Crum die infinitely if elected.

fans/card-king.title: Card King
fans/card-king.content:
Card King
Card King (cardking_01 on Twitch, which AI Rooney reads out as “Card King underscore zero one”) has been in Case’s chat since at least December 2023 and is named in more than 160 broadcasts. They’re a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
Card King is one of the channel’s steadiest supporters. They gift community subs in batches, cheer hundreds of bits at a time, and get greeted in the opening roll call. Their cheers come with messages, and since mid-2024 those messages have been read aloud in the president’s voice. They have also sent Clementine a conspiracy to investigate, requested Munch & Crum debates and a DJ C4 song, written rhymes that broke Scrum, fed four complaints to AI Rooney, and shared a steady supply of clips for Amongst the Web. Case also reads a lot of their chat out on air, including the one comment that made Kendelle walk off.
Listen Up, Jack
On 2024-05-15, Case switched on a new alert: any cheer over 300 bits gets its message read out by text-to-speech in a Joe Biden voice. The template is “Listen up, Jack. Card King just mama-jammed 300 shiny tasty coins, and I’ve been dying to say this,” followed by whatever the viewer typed. The transcripts often garble it into “Card King unjust mama jam.” “Just Mama Jam” is part of the alert, not another chatter; the same wording comes before every cheerer’s name (Microphone 900, Skymer, Giggle Trash, Big J Dub and others).
Card King’s was the second alert ever. Biden recited “Jenny from the Block” (“They know where I came from, from the Bronx”), and Case decided, “I think I like this text-to-speech thing actually, it’s providing the chaos.” Since then Card King has used the president for dozens of interruptions. Biden has rapped for Jeb’s rack-chugging initiation (“the president literally demanded it”), urged Hype Train to “torch the field” and “fuck Jeff Ripple” (Jeff: “That train has it out for me”), slipped acid into Pepito’s birthday cheese, outed Hate Sock, announced “I’ve hijacked the presidency,” asked for “triple dancing Kendelles,” called Kendelle to the stand at Crum’s mock trial, and recited a prayer on a How To with Jeb. Case usually answers “What’s that, Mr. President?”, and once thanked “Mr. President slash Card King” for the bits.
A 1,000-bit cheer triggers a bigger version: “Card King underscore zero one just absolutely pounded 1,000 sweet bits straight into the great chasm of progress, and I just have to say this.” On 2025-12-11 it brought out Obama (“Yo, Joe, sit the hell down and let a real president hold it down”), and Case thanked Card King “for summoning the very secret president.”
Requests
Card King’s suggestions turn into segments fairly often. On 2024-03-14, Clementine investigated the House of Illuminati, the firm behind the Glasgow Willy Wonka experience, at Card King’s request. Card King dropped the Wayback Machine link and Clementine thanked them for it: “You said it was silly. I’ll say it was anything but silly. I’m deeply disturbed.” A week later, 1,000 bits bought the Munch & Crum debate “When AI achieves consciousness, will they leave ghosts when they die?” (2024-03-21). Card King requested DJ C4’s Celtic dubstep track “Rockin’ in the Green Screen” on 2025-05-23, a Royal Rumble watch-along, and the “How to Crip Walk for Beginners” lesson on 2026-11-04.

fans/live-in-sleazy.title: Live 'n Sleazy
fans/live-in-sleazy.content:
Live ‘n Sleazy
Live ‘n Sleazy (usually heard as “Live in Sleazy” or “Live and Sleazy”) is one of Case’s two “master mods,” alongside Sabreche. They’ve been in chat since at least November 2023 (“Live and Sleazy, the other master mod… The best mod in the business is both of them”) and are named on air in about 250 broadcasts through November 2026. They’re a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
Sleazy is the chatter Case trusts on facts. He regularly takes their word over his own (“if it’s from Live in Sleazy it is always a real answer”), tracks down the clip or article he’s fumbling for, and jokes that they know where things are in his house better than he does. They’re also the most frequent source of Amongst the Web submissions, which Case treats as a gamble. Off the news desk, they handle mod chores like making Discord threads and running polls, helped Case spec and build his streaming PC, send Brandon the games and ROMs he plays, and have made assets and AI videos for the show. They request segments (a Munch & Crum debate, How To with Jeb, the rarely run AI Rooney) and songs for DJ C4. From October 2025 on, AI Rooney opens a long run of rants with “Live and Sleazy got me thinking,” covering condom sizes (2025-11-27), pythons going for your grundle (2026-04-24), vapes (2026-04-27), $120 hot dogs (2026-05-04), shaving (2026-05-12) and soup that’s too spicy (2026-06-22).
The Live in Sleazy Dice
Because so many Amongst the Web clips come from Sleazy, and they range from great to deliberately awful, Case started introducing them as a roll of the dice. “Let’s end with a submission from Live and Sleazy. Meaning it could be incredible, or we could intentionally end on a terrible one… It’s all up to the whims of Live and Sleazy” (2025-08-02). Later versions: “he might punish us or reward us. It’s really at Live in Sleazy’s discretion” (2025-12-04); “Live and Sleazy is a knife or a massage, and you never know what you’ll get” (2025-12-09); “It’s like a Targaryen being born or whatever. The world sees a new clip from Live in Sleazy and holds their breath” (2025-12-18). Sleazy has become the yardstick: fellow chatter Psychor is “almost a Live and Sleazy level savant when it comes to rolling the dice on video quality” (2026-01-27).
The usual punishment for a bad clip, “ban the submitter,” doesn’t work on a mod. On 2025-01-15, after Sleazy posted a Marjorie Taylor Greene video that chat rated a zero, Case ran a poll on whether Sleazy should ban themselves. Chat filled in the options, and “self suck” won: “Live in Sleazy, we’ll give you a couple months to take the necessary yoga classes, but that is your punishment for posting that Marjorie Taylor Greene video.” By 2025-04-04 the rule was settled: “you can only get Live and Sleazy to ban themselves. Or you have to make Live and Sleazy and Sabreche go to war with each other. Nobody wants that.”
Mod Work and Tech Help
Case relies on Sleazy for the parts of running a stream he doesn’t understand. When he asked whether they could make threads in the Discord, “Live and Sleazy is the hero we need and he’s already made it” (2025-05-13). fans/matt-liddell.title: Matt Liddell
fans/matt-liddell.content:
Matt Liddell
Matt Liddell (matt_liddell on Twitch) has been in Case’s chat since at least November 2023, and his name comes up in more than 100 broadcasts. He’s a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
He is one of the channel’s longest-running subscribers: Case counted 28 months on 2025-03-31 and 33 on 2025-09-13 (“Matt Liddell, one of the OGs”), and he had a 70-stream watch streak by 2026-11-07. On air he is best known as the one chatter reliably in Crum’s corner, which got him blamed for Crum’s election wins in Rennerton. He is also the subject of a long-running bit that started with a “Matt Liddell tie” and ended with Case and the correspondents wearing temporary tattoos of his face. Along the way the cast has made him Case’s tax attorney, Crum’s “accountant attorney,” Brandon’s unwanted stepdad, and the namesake of Brandon’s Final Fantasy XIV catboy. On 2026-02-28 he was greeted as “Matt Liddell, the man of a thousand muscle faces. I think that’s Matt Liddell’s nickname. It is to me.”
The Matt Liddell Tattoo
It started as a tie. During the fish-tie debate on 2025-05-21, chat floated “a Matt Liddell tie,” and Case wondered what that would even mean: “Would it be like a little Matt Liddell, a full-body Matt Liddell just as a tie?” Matt endorsed the idea later that stream. Nine months later he turned up on Trip on the Street (2026-02-12) to ask after it: “There was supposed to be a tie made in my visage… When do I get my royalties?” Trip promised to raise it with Case: “Honestly, I hope he pays you. Fuck that guy.”
Five days later (2026-02-17), chat’s suggestions for Case’s first tattoo landed on Matt. “I’m getting a Matt Liddell tie and a Matt Liddell tattoo. Why? Why do I need so much Matt Liddell on my body?” Case agreed to pay for a cutout tie if someone could design one, but drew the line elsewhere: “I am not getting a nude Matt Liddell apron. It feels like it’s in bad taste. To Matt.” On 2026-03-12 the tattoo became a sub goal. Case insisted “I’m not getting the permanent Matt Liddell tattoo” and settled on custom temporary ones, while Hype Train rapped about forcing “a Matt Liddell on your face.” Matt sent in photos (“These are the Matt options, everyone”) and Case asked Kendelle to wear one with him (2026-03-19). On 2026-04-06, Crum demanded, “Where’s the fucking Matt Liddell tattoo?… I feel like I’m the only one who remembers this shit, Case.”
The tattoos arrived in a pack of ten, and Case applied the first one on air in a sleeveless undershirt on “Casual Friday,” 2026-05-01: “It’s fucking huge… Maybe I was being too optimistic about the size of my arms.” Jeff, Chet and Kendelle got matching ones. Chet insisted “my Matt tattoo looks even better.” The next day “we had the guns out today to show off the Matt tat,” and Case joked that a permanent version is “priority number one” (2026-05-02). When the much cheaper Bart Simpson temporary tattoos turned out to be hard to get off, he looked back fondly: “Obviously I went with only the most premium Matt Liddell tattoo” (2026-08-26).
Crum’s Constituency
While the rest of chat was cheering for the Rock-afire gorilla in the Crum Face Punch bet, Munch grumbled on 2025-06-11 that Crum had “one defender… I respect Matt Liddell and his commitment to pacifism, but everybody else wants to see you fucking die.” Crum: “It’s more than just Matt. There’s a whole Crum pack.” After the punch, Matt left Munch a threat on Trip on the Street, and in the debut of Encircled he challenged Munch over Crum’s death. Munch called him “the most formidable adversary.” On 2026-03-10 Crum thanked him “for taking back this station for the people who founded it, me and you, Matt.” By 2026-09-02, Matt was posting in chat as “Crum’s accountant attorney,” and when Crum threatened to sue chat on 2026-11-05 he made an exception: “Not all of you, obviously not Matt Liddell.”
That loyalty carried into the Rebuild Rennerton elections, which run on unlimited channel-points polls (“It is pay to play. One vote, one dollar”). When Crum beat skeleton Munch for mayor on 2026-11-06, Munch knew who to blame: “You guys keep fucking doing this to yourselves, and by you guys I do mean you, Matt. I mean specifically Matt Liddell.” At Mayor Crum’s first press conference the next day, Matt checked in before going to pick up dinner (“You’re doing an awesome job”). Crum: “Always happy to have your support. What a gosh darn hero.” When Crum took an early lead in that evening’s election, Case said, “I don’t even know if Matt Liddell’s around, so I can’t tell if that’s the usual pay to play that Crum engages in to win these elections.” Melody Von Torture won anyway, and Case told the new mayor: “No matter what the Matt Liddell constituency says, you’ve always been my mayor.” Crum’s parting words in his concession: “Matt, I know you got the points. Come on. Let’s not let it slip.”

fans/melody-von-torture.title: Melody Von Torture
fans/melody-von-torture.content:
Melody Von Torture
Melody Von Torture (MVT) has been in Case’s chat since at least July 2024. They’re a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
MVT is one of the broadcast’s most hands-on chatters. They built a playable Mega Man fan game starring Case, drew a stack of the Bart Simpson tattoo designs, submitted merch, supplied AI Rooney with complaints, sent requests to Brandon, and became one of the first citizens of the Rebuild Rennerton Valheim server. On 2026-11-07, chat elected them mayor of Rennerton over Crum.
Mega Case
On 2026-04-11, Case spent most of the broadcast in Amongst the Web playing a Mega Man fan game MVT made about him. In it, Mega-Case sets out to rescue Chet from evil robots, armed with a communicator that is “also a gun” and a “Bin Buster.” MVT built it to be easy for Case to set up (“They truly went above and beyond”). Case: “Melody Von Torture, you have truly outdone yourself. I don’t know what to say.”
The first level took him about an hour. He farmed extra lives off respawning enemies to avoid replaying the opening section (“We’re cheating the system, guys”), and called MVT an “evil bastard” when the boss turned out to be the only thing in the game that does real damage. After finally beating it, he said: “Melody Von Torture, it’s fair that you made it that hard, because if there were like 10 more of those levels, I would literally be here all night… Some of my best voice acting work ever I did for this game. Melody Von Torture, truly too kind to make an actual game for me, of me, a game of me for me. And at just the right skill level to make me play one level for an hour. You know me too well.” He offered to record voice lines or sing over the chiptunes for a sequel, and read out the game’s credits (“look at you actually crediting people, something I never do on the stream”). Kendelle and Crum tried it too; Crum quit after one death. Case shouted out the game again on 2026-04-14.
Mayor of Rennerton
MVT was the first citizen to join the Rennerton Valheim server on 2026-10-23 (“Welcome to the town, MVT”). They soon found the press corps (“Oh my god, it’s MVT! You’ve made it!”), and their gathered resources paid for skeleton Munch’s mayoral mansion: “Fortunately, the bounties of Melody Von Torture and Exterminator have provided for us.”
They came back on 2026-11-06 with Stanton “to save the day,” and Munch ranked the pair top of the town’s citizens. Once Crum took over as mayor, he fell into a hole MVT had dug: “Melody Von Torture, how could you do this to me?” The next day, MVT out-worked him again (“That was all MVT?”), and he admitted, “I’m not mad at you for digging holes. I’ve just been falling into them.” At the end of that stream, MVT stood for mayor against Crum and Peter. Crum led the early count with 97 votes, but “as the more Melody Von Torture centered counties” came in, Big News called the race for MVT. Crum conceded through gritted teeth: “I am so excited for my new mayor Melody Von Torture… I’m excited to work as a key advisor to Melody Von Torture to see his agenda through.”

fans/propaganda.title: Propaganda
fans/propaganda.content:
Propaganda
Propaganda (propaganda_v2 on Twitch) has been in Case’s chat since at least late 2023, and is named on air in more than a hundred broadcasts. They’re a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
Case usually just says “Propaganda.” When the full handle comes up, AI Rooney reads it as “propaganda underscore v2.” They’re a multi-year subscriber (Case has read out everything from 21 months to 42), a VIP since 2026-06-01, a regular in the opening roll call, and one of the chat’s steadiest sources of clips, expert requests and Rooney complaints. On 2026-11-13, Case briefly crowned them “the lore master himself” before correcting the record: that title belongs to Teflon Ted; Propaganda is “lore master number two, or archivist.”
Lore Master Number Two, or Archivist
Propaganda’s name is a running joke on the desk (“Propaganda, my favorite thing to spread and one of my favorite names to see here,” 2025-04-23), and they lean into the archivist role. They keep feeding the broadcast old clips, Discord art and wiki nudges. On 2024-10-30, Case stopped mid-stream for “a huge shout out to Propaganda for making this” Discord piece. On 2026-07-20: “Propaganda, thank you for the clips as always.” And on 2026-11-13, while co-hosting Amongst the Web with Jevrything, Case opened Propaganda’s throwback with “the lore master himself,” then immediately demoted them:

Well, technically that’s Teflon Ted. Lore master number two, or archivist.

Propaganda is also the chatter other people ping when something needs checking. Case has told the room to “ask Propaganda,” credited them with beating him to a Greta Thunberg clip, and trusted them with the cream.team link at sign-off (“There you go, Propaganda has it,” 2026-11-12).
Amongst the Web
Propaganda is a recurring submitter. Their clips show up in the queue whether or not Case remembers who sent them:

2025-01-22: “Propaganda video. Let’s just see what it is.”
2026-06-29: Listed among the night’s contributors (with Sleazy, Psychor and Uncle Phil) before the queue “veered into the piss genre.”
2026-09-23: “Look at this video coming in from propaganda. This looks crazy.”
2026-10-29: “Coming all the way in… from Propaganda.”
2026-11-13: The throwback that earned the archivist title.

”Propaganda Underscore V2 Got Me Thinking”
Propaganda has fed at least 14 complaints to AI Rooney between 2025-10-02 and 2026-06-29. Rooney almost always opens with the handle before agreeing and drifting. The complaints include corkboards as “flesh-ridden relics,” Thanksgiving as a “piss-fast,” soft burger buns that need “a foot right there in the mix,” condoms as “an unaffordable tax” for Spin City viewing, pizzeria arcades that used to run Metal Slug 3, babies in ninja gear, Nights into Dreams’ Jester, and the sitcom Wings. On 2026-06-03, Rooney got as far as the catchphrase before blanking: “Well quick wait. I forgot what I was complaining about. My brain is empty. You son of a bitch.”

fans/skymer.title: Skymer
fans/skymer.content:
Skymer
Skymer (skymyr on Twitch) has been in Case’s chat since at least November 2023 and is named on air in more than 200 broadcasts. They’re a viewer, not a character, so this page is filed under Fanatical Fans rather than On-Air Talent.
Skymer is a long-time subscriber (Case read out 35 months in October 2025 and 36 in May 2026), a steady source of 100-, 300- and 1,000-bit cheers, and a regular in Case’s opening roll calls and sign-off raps. Their bits have summoned the presidential bit alert about 20 times, and their chat lines get read on the desk, turned into AI Rooney complaints, and used against Crum. They once called in live to Guy Redacted, and in May 2026 Case made them a VIP. Even after all that, nobody on the show can agree on how to say the name.
Summoning the President
A 300-bit cheer sets off an alert in Joe Biden’s voice: “Listen up, Jack. Skymer just mama-jammed 300 shiny tasty coins, and I’ve been dying to say this,” followed by whatever the president has to say. At 1,000 bits Barack Obama turns up instead: “Skymer just absolutely pounded 1,000 sweet bits straight into the great chasm of progress.” Skymer has set these off around 20 times since May 2024:

2024-07-15, six days before the real Biden dropped out: “I’m stepping aside so Hype Train can be our new nominee.” (“I graciously accept. I’m now running for president.“)
2025-06-11, Case’s birthday: Biden: “Happy birthday, young man. I remember when I was your age.” Later, Obama: “I’m already in SEAL Team 6 to take out Crum.”
2025-12-18: While Case is struggling to get the Hype Train to appear, Biden turns up to plug “my sweet plaque at the White House.” Case: “Thank you so much, Mr. President, for your kind words, and Skymer for summoning the president. Today we are all Skymer.”
2026-03-07: In the middle of Crum’s mock trial, Obama arrives on Skymer’s 1,000 bits: “Ladies and gentlemen, we got him. Our long national nightmare is over. Fuck Crum.”
2026-07-24: Obama brings back Obamacare to treat Case’s ankle injury, though because of budget cuts it’s “mostly a thoughts and prayers based treatment.” Case: “Skymer, far too kind with the thousand bits that’ll go straight into the thoughts and prayers fund for my ankle.”

Shut Up, Crum
Skymer’s messages are a reliable source of material against Crum, and Munch reads them out gladly. “Yes, gross Crum. Thank you, Skymer” (2024-03-01). Skymer suggested the insult “J.K. Crum rolling,” and Crum himself admitted it was “more fun to say” (2024-08-01). Munch thanked Skymer for apologizing “for anyone having to see Crum” (2025-02-12), and in a debate over baby photos agreed with their theory that Crum “was in a cocoon from most of his childhood” (“That sounds right, Skymer,” 2025-12-09). While Crum was supposed to be awaiting his dick punch, chat, “and particularly Skymer,” wanted to know: “Why aren’t you dead yet, Crum?” (2026-03-19, see Crum Dick Punch). More recently: “Point is, shut up, Crum. Skymer gets it” (2026-07-13); “Yes, absolutely, Skymer, give him Havana syndrome” (2026-09-01); and at skeleton Munch’s Rennerton press conference, a “great point, Skymer” about how to stop future Crum attacks: “the answer is 100% execute Crum” (2026-11-06).

index.content:
BIN Lore
The comprehensive broadcast archive and newsroom record for Barely Informed News — the premier satirical broadcast network anchored by Case Blackwell.
This archive documents the network’s on-air correspondents, investigative programming, evolving newsroom storylines, and complete broadcast telecasts as they unfold live on air.

Fan Site Notice: BIN Lore is an independent, non-commercial fan documentation project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Case Blackwell, Barely Informed News, or Twitch. All trademarks, names, likenesses, and broadcast assets belong to their respective copyright holders and are referenced under fair use for commentary, criticism, and archival purposes. Not operated for profit. See the full Legal & Fan Disclaimer.

Network Directory

On-Air Talent — anchors, senior correspondents, debate analysts, and production crew
Fanatical Fans — chatters, moderators, and superfans whose names keep making it onto the broadcast
Broadcast Segments — signature programming, remote dispatches, and regular desks
Events & Story Arcs — marathon specials, annual events, and multi-episode newsroom sagas
Commercial Sponsors — corporate partners, fast-casual underwriters, and commercial dispatches
Episodes & Broadcast Archive — complete broadcast catalog and episode logs
Schedule Report Card — Mon/Wed/Fri attendance grades (affectionate, curved)

Featured Coverage
The Crum Dick Punch saga — alongside the high-stakes Munch & Crum debate desk — remains the central developing storyline across the network. Start with senior analysts Crum and Ralph Munchcut. Marathon specials include Rennerton, Deb-8, and the annual Grunchmas.
Network Transmissions
Barely Informed News broadcasts live on Twitch (caseblackwell), with complete historical archives preserved on YouTube (CaseBlackwellStreams). BIN Lore exists to maintain complete institutional memory across all network dispatches.
Contributing
Notice missing broadcast lore, an unrecorded correspondent appearance, or a detail requiring editorial correction? Network contributions are warmly welcomed! Please feel free to submit a pull request on GitHub with your suggested updates or additions. Sourced notes with broadcast dates and timestamps are especially appreciated.
Legal Disclaimer
This wiki is operated strictly as a non-commercial, non-profit community fan archive under the Fair Use doctrine (17 U.S.C. § 107). No copyright or trademark infringement is intended. All broadcast elements and trademarks remain the property of Case Blackwell / Barely Informed News. Read our complete Legal & Fan Disclaimer for non-affiliation, fair use, parody, and takedown policy details.

schedule/index.title: Schedule Report Card
schedule/index.content:
Schedule Report Card
Case Blackwell advertises a tidy Monday / Wednesday / Friday Barely Informed News schedule. The episode catalog tells a warmer, messier story.
This page grades advertised-slot attendance only — did a wiki episode land on that calendar Mon, Wed, or Fri? Bonus Tuesday chaos is celebrated separately. Figures are computed from ingested episode dates (2023-11-22 → 2026-10-19, 342 distinct broadcast days).

House curve: BIN does not use your high school’s grading scale. Clearing 40% of Fridays is already a solid C. Mondays are graded on a spiritual curve and still somehow fail.

Report card



































CourseAttendanceRateGradeMonday (Honors)43/15228.3%F — Theoretical broadcast dayWednesday (Elective)57/15237.5%D — Sighted in the wildFriday (Core)63/15241.4%C — Fridays-adjacent competenceMWF composite163/45635.7%D — Sighted in the wild
Term GPA: 1.0 / 4.00
(Average of the three day-letter GPAs. Extra-credit Tue/Thu streams do not inflate this number, no matter how hard they try.)
Teacher’s comments

Valedictorian of the trifecta: Friday — the day most likely to actually happen.
Needs improvement: Monday — frequently excused by vibes, travel, sty, or “next week for sure.”
Hidden curriculum: Across the whole archive the busiest broadcast weekdays are Thursday (68) and Tuesday (64), with Friday (63) close behind. Monday (43) remains the rarest weekday on the books. The real schedule appears to be “whenever the newsroom assembles,” with Friday as the closest thing to a promise.
Last 12 months: MWF hit rate 30.6% (Mon 30.2% · Wed 26.9% · Fri 34.6%); 56 non-MWF bonus shows. Even the recent form guide agrees — Fridays lead, Mondays sulk, Wednesdays flip a coin and then pocket it.

Extra credit
Case does not owe the universe a sparse calendar. 179 catalogued broadcasts landed on Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun in this window — more “off-schedule” shows than successful Mondays (43). Truancy on the brochure; overachievement in the lab.

Methodology

Collect distinct date: values from content/episodes/*.md (filename date used if frontmatter is missing).
Enumerate every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from the earliest episode through the latest.
A hit is any advertised slot that has at least one ingested episode that day.
Regenerated with ./binlore schedule-report (writes this page + data/schedule-report.json).

This is affectionate scorekeeping, not a HR file. Streams get cancelled for holidays, travel, illness, apartment moves, Thailand arcs, and the occasional mechanical gorilla. The joke is the brochure — the catalog is the punchline.

AI Rooney

The audience-prompted grievance commentary desk on Barely Informed News, hosted by the network’s proprietary cyborg commentator, AI Rooney.
Format
Conceived as a computational homage to CBS 60 Minutes commentator Andy Rooney, the AI Rooney segment featured lead anchor Case Blackwell activating the newsroom’s resident cyborg to deliver deadpan, escalating, 60 Minutes-style diatribes and rants on topics submitted in real time by viewers via stream chat commands (such as !rr).
Key Elements

Host — AI Rooney: Proprietary cyborg commentator delivering Andy Rooney–style grievance essays.
Homage to Andy Rooney: The segment mirrored the cadence, rhetorical questions, and curmudgeonly skepticism of Andy Rooney’s legendary 60 Minutes closing essays, applied to surreal modern annoyances.
Audience-Submitted Topics: Viewers prompted the cyborg with topics ranging from sitcom trivia and cultural oddities to everyday household grievances.
Escalation & Muting: Over time, the cyborg’s internal algorithmic guardrails deteriorated. Rooney’s rants escalated into increasingly unhinged, caustic, and volatile territory (including diatribes against Wings, mutated Ninja Turtle babies, and massage gun eye injuries), forcing Case Blackwell to repeatedly slap the mute button live on air.
Indefinite Retirement: During the 2026-07-13 broadcast, a localized model malfunction caused Rooney to emit explicit offensive content and slurs on the air. Blackwell pulled the plug on the segment mid-stream, and following an on-air debate between staff and analysts, the network permanently retired the segment and decommissioned the cyborg.

Amongst the Web

The audience-interactive viral media review desk on Barely Informed News.
Format
Case Blackwell is the only consistent host of Amongst the Web, joined by a different co-host each time to watch, evaluate, and react to viewer-submitted video evidence, internet phenomena, and digital subculture clips gathered from the community Discord. The hosts rate and dissect each submission while the live chat audience participates with real-time commentary and sentiment.
Key Elements

Anchor & Rotating Co-Hosts: Case Blackwell anchors every broadcast, while his co-host rotates each session—featuring recurring personalities and special guests such as tactical media correspondent Rick, the eccentric Marfus Darfus, solar-laser enthusiast Grandma Crumble Bottom, or chaotic desk hijackings by studio stowaway Peter Gibbon.
Viewer Submissions: Videos are sourced directly from the audience via the community Discord’s “amongst this web” queue in the BIN news section.
Idiosyncratic Ratings: The hosts frequently assign peculiar or hyper-specific decimal scores to each clip (such as Marfus Darfus’s landmark 6.44 rating).
Focus: Surreal internet culture, odd viral recordings, awkward cringe clips, and community-submitted oddities.

segments/at-the-movies.title: At the Movies
segments/at-the-movies.content:
At the Movies

The recurring movie-trailer review desk on Barely Informed News, usually billed on-air as Trent at the Movies or Trailer Thursday.
Format
Field correspondent Trent — a truant teen of deliberately ambiguous age — hosts from a green-screen movie theater while his probation officer Chris supervises (and argues) from the same “BIN movie theater” bit. The pair screen trailers, assign half-serious ratings, and digress into genre fights, green-screen safety lectures, and parole logistics.
Key Elements

Trent (Young Blood): Self-styled cultural taste-maker and movie correspondent; long hair lore, beanie-and-blazer theater look, contractual “fire transition” when the desk allows.
Chris (Probation Officer): Required on-set supervision for Trent’s community-service broadcast work; co-hosts reviews, undercuts Trent’s takes, and occasionally hijacks the mic.
Trailer Block: Several trailers per appearance (studio, indie, game-adjacent, and deeply cursed), often with chat rating schemes.
Alias Soup: Same desk appears as Trailer Thursday, Trailer Time, Trend at the Movies, Go to the Movies, and plain At the Movies.

segments/banter.title: Banter
segments/banter.content:
Banter
Unscripted desk chatter between Case Blackwell, in-studio talent and chat: pre-show warm-ups, technical setup, housekeeping and schedule talk, and loose conversation between segments. Not news coverage and not gameplay.
Format
Case talks directly with chat and whoever is in the studio, usually Kendelle, Pepito or Crum. Banter fills the gaps the rundown doesn’t: troubleshooting the stream, thanking subscribers, planning the night’s segments, plugging the schedule, and wandering off-topic.
Key Elements

Pre-show and technical setup: audio checks, scene fixes, mods and lobby setup before the first real segment.
Housekeeping: stream schedule, Kickstarter and Patreon plugs, sub goals, segment planning.
Desk chat: personal stories, chat polls and tangents between segments.

What isn’t Banter

Headline coverage, chat news and wire roundups belong to News, as do the cold open and the sign-off.
Gameplay belongs to Gaming, or to CryptoZeu$ when Brandon is playing.

See also: News, Gaming, Broadcast Segments.

segments/chet-guy-the-science-eyes.content:
Chet Guy the Science Eyes

The specialized investigative science and medical research desk on Barely Informed News, anchored by Chief Science Correspondent Chet (Chet Manscape) alongside synthetic neural co-host ChetAI.
Format
The segment operates under a strict, spontaneous network trigger protocol: whenever any anchor, reporter, or correspondent across the broadcast utters the trigger words “science” or “scientist,” Chet immediately intervenes to commandeer the news desk. Sporting specialized blue-light-filtering eyewear, Chet deploys a high-powered laboratory optical microscope directly onto the desk.

Conspiracy Desk

The recurring conspiracy deep-dive desk on Barely Informed News, variously billed as Conspiracy Time, Truth Zone, or a handoff to correspondent Guy Redacted.
Format
Case (or a designated conspiracy correspondent) opens a YouTube rabbit hole — blueberries that “aren’t blue,” Saturnalia Christmas psyops, secret turtles, Bigfoot thank-you notes — and commits to the bit until the evidence collapses into parody. Later seasons formalize the desk around Guy Redacted, who operates from an “undisclosed location” after periods of on-air censorship.
Key Elements

Conspiracy Time / Truth Zone: Named cold-open for the desk before and alongside Guy Redacted’s tenure.
Guy Redacted: Sunglasses-forward conspiracy correspondent; Illuminati-hat era returns; investigates Avril Lavigne replacements, Giza underground cities, and blueberry color scandals.
Prior host — Clementine Verne: Original Conspiracy Time / Unvernished Truth correspondent (curly-wigged man) before Guy Redacted’s desk branding.
Chat as research assistants: Viewers dump links; the desk treats ten-view uploads as primary sources.

segments/cryptozeus.content:
CryptoZeu$

The live remote video game and digital culture dispatch on Barely Informed News, anchored by gaming correspondent Brandon (CryptoZeu$).
Format
Broadcasting remote from his private bedroom studio, Brandon conducts deep-dive playthroughs and historical evaluations of vintage computer games—frequently vintage MS-DOS platformers (such as Epic MegaGames’ Jill of the Jungle trilogy) and simulation classics (such as RollerCoaster Tycoon).
Brandon’s gameplay is consistently disrupted by his mother shouting through the closed bedroom door with an exasperated, muffled voice. The mother’s dialogue is sourced directly from incoming viewer submissions and community correspondence, and she invariably berates him as “Bran Bran.”
Key Elements

Host — Brandon (CryptoZeu$): Gaming correspondent conducting remote playthroughs from his bedroom studio.
Muffled Hallway Inquiries: Brandon’s mother interrogates him regarding household affairs, neighborhood gossip, and questionable dietary practices.
“Bran Bran”: The universal maternal address used on the broadcast.
Narrative Improvisation: Brandon reconstructs elaborate historical mythologies based on shareware menus and environmental textures.
Corporate Sponsor Updates: Live commercial advisories on behalf of regional culinary partner Gooters, advertising chicken wings and “dino fries.”

segments/dj-c4.title: DJ C4
segments/dj-c4.content:
DJ C4

The in-studio musical production and collaborative songwriting segment on Barely Informed News, hosted by resident composer and producer DJ C4 from the DJC4 Studios.
Format & Overview
Broadcasting live from the wood-paneled DJC4 Studios, DJ C4 takes control of the network feed to compose original songs, segment theme tracks, and promotional anthems in real time. Rather than relying solely on pre-recorded instrumentation, the segment combines live beat production, audience interaction, and generative AI ghostwriting tools.
Throughout the session, viewers participate directly by submitting lyrical couplets, headlines, and comedic concepts through the chat command !L to send a lyric. DJ C4 synthesizes these lines with AI assistance to generate melodic hooks, verse arrangements, and full-length network tracks—often drafting on-air correspondents into the vocal booth for live guest verses.
Key Elements

Host — DJ C4 / DJC4 Studio Setting: Anchored from a dedicated soundstage adorned with studio monitors, audio racks, and glowing amber-yellow neon signage.
AI-Assisted Songwriting: Direct collaboration between DJ C4 and AI ghostwriting models to arrange chords, harmonies, and rhymes in response to chat prompts.
Interactive Lyric Crowdsourcing (!L): Live intake of viewer-generated lyrics, allowing the broadcast audience to steer the subject matter of network anthems.
Theme Composition for Correspondents: Producing customized walkout themes, segment intros, and sonic branding for newsroom talent.
Guest Features & Reluctant Rappers: Bringing in network personalities—such as senior debate analyst Crum—to record rap features and pre-emptive marital disclaimers.

Known Occurrences















EpisodeTimestampNotes2026-07-171:47:57DJC4 ‘Free Stephanie’ Merch Drop Anthem: DJ C4 assembles a live merch-drop single using AI ghostwriting, pivoting from a request by Live ‘n Sleazy (‘the economy ceasefire violation blues’) into the ‘Free Stephanie’ track. Crum performs a Crum-style rap (‘get on my mug or a hot butt plug’) with an anxious pre-emptive fidelity disclaimer to his wife Belolia.
See also: DJ C4 (Character), DJ Newsic, Crum, Case Blackwell, Broadcast Segments.

segments/dj-newsic.title: DJ Newsic
segments/dj-newsic.content:
DJ Newsic

The signature auto-tuned electronic musical finale on Barely Informed News, hosted by resident blue-haired DJ DJ Newsic to sing the news over driving techno beats and close out broadcasts.
Format & Overview
Emerging directly at the anchor desk, DJ Newsic takes over the broadcast to deliver a pulse-pounding, high-BPM musical news digest. Armed with heavy vocal auto-tune and driving techno tracks, DJ Newsic sings headlines and fast-tracks bizarre, offbeat stories that regular anchor Case Blackwell skipped or was “too afraid to click on” earlier in the show.
The segment bridges political satire and club-ready electronic performance, turning controversial domestic reports, viral international incidents, and oddity news wires into melodic techno anthems before sending the stream off to its concluding raid.
Key Elements

DJ Newsic (Blue-Haired News Anchor): Presides over the desk with a distinctive bright electric blue wig and reflective sunglasses.
Heavy Auto-Tuned News Delivery: Every headline, lyric, and audience response is filtered through thick, pitch-corrected auto-tune.
Driving Techno Instrumentals: Fast-paced synth loops and techno basslines keep the tempo exhilarating as the broadcast sprints to a close.
Unclicked Story Coverage: Focuses specifically on eccentric, uncomfortable, or legally precarious stories that Case Blackwell bypassed during the main news block.
Surreal Musical Guests: Impromptu appearances by unexpected remote guests—including talking animals and anthropomorphic interviewees—who contribute their own musical perspectives.

Known Occurrences

He covers a South Korean Michelin-starred restaurant facing prosecution for using ants as a dessert garnish, passionately sings that ‘love is the only ingredient that should be legal’, and interviews an elephant guest who performs an outrageous closing musical number.

segments/encircled.title: Encircled
segments/encircled.content:
Encircled

Encircled is the last-one-standing debate gauntlet on Barely Informed News: one defender stakes out a claim and must hold it against a seemingly endless line of random challengers. Chat votes each challenger out by spamming !rf (red flag). When enough red flags land, the challenger drops into a deep pit and the next one sits down.
Format

The intro sting: Every edition opens with the same montage of “past defenders” stating their odd stances: “I just think soda’s better without ice. I just think you should be dead. Music is bad and it’s bad for you. What? A sock on the door means a crime is happening. Okay, but I don’t really get where I am.” Oddly, the voices in the montage are well-known primary characters, while the real defenders are almost always off-the-cuff random characters. Once the sting ends, that random defender appears, usually confused about where they are.
The premise: Each Encircled has its own matchup title on screen (e.g. Case vs 30 Unpaid Interns, 1 dumbass vs 30 dumbasses), almost always one versus 30. The topic, the defender, and the opposition change every time, and many matchups come from chat segment requests.
The claim: The defender’s position is pinned on screen as CLAIM:. Early editions (Munch, Crum, Kevin) used three claims; later ones settle on one. Viewers submit challenges with !cc (counter claim), and Case confirms each one in chat (“Counter claim encircled, brace for random selection”). The selected counter shows on screen as COUNTER:, and a fresh random character arrives to argue it.
The vote: A RED FLAGS banner (“!RF votes challenger out”) marks voting. Once the flags pile up, an announcer declares the challenger “voted out by the group” and they fall down the hole, usually still arguing on the way down.
The clock: A countdown timer sits between the two chairs. When it runs out, the announcer calls “Okay, pause, that’s time. Please wait in your seat.” If the defender is still seated, they survive. The timer has a history of glitching.
Hosts who don’t know the name: Defenders routinely fumble the title. Crum welcomes everyone “back to… Circled. Being told that’s what it’s called,” and Chet notes “nobody ever introduces this segment.”
Exit methods: The pit is the current way out. Earlier editions used a fire trap (2025-09-13) and an incinerator chute (2026-04-14).

Known occurrences

Gaming
Live gameplay on the main broadcast by Case Blackwell, in-studio talent and guests, from co-op sessions to game browsing. Brandon’s remote retro playthroughs are a separate segment, CryptoZeu$.
Format
Case takes the broadcast into a game, often with a co-op lobby of studio regulars and guest streamers. Sessions have included Lethal Company (including the Great Lethal Off), Elden Ring, Peak and Shift at Midnight. Trent has also played solo runs. Chat suggests titles, and Case browses the store live when picking the next game.
Key Elements

Co-op lobbies: Case with Kendelle, Crum, Pepito and guest streamers.
Setup on air: mod configuration, Discord calls and lobby troubleshooting are part of the session.
Game browsing: reviewing store pages and chat recommendations before committing to a game.

What isn’t Gaming

Brandon’s bedroom-studio playthroughs are always CryptoZeu$.
The Valheim rebuild of Rennerton is Rebuild Rennerton.
Small talk before or after a session is Banter.

segments/how-to-with-jeb.title: How To with Jeb
segments/how-to-with-jeb.content:
How To with Jeb

How To with Jeb is a rogue instructional broadcast segment on Barely Informed News, hosted by Jeb Nogget alongside his deceased father, whose spirit is trapped within a wooden board.
Format & Overview
Broadcasting without warning from an unkempt woodworking shop, How To with Jeb masquerades as an earnest, educational instructional show designed to teach viewers practical life skills. In reality, the broadcast serves as an uncomfortable psychological battleground between Jeb and his co-hosting father—a literal piece of wood possessed by the elder Nogget’s restless, critical soul.
Despite broadcasting from a workshop, Jeb admits he possesses no raw logs, working entirely with pre-cut wood while cryptically citing an unspecified “mechanism” that grants him innate woodworking mastery. Rather than standard crafting, the segment frequently derails into external tutorial videos spanning self-defense, martial escapes, and suggestive nightclub dancing.
The Cohost & Family Lore
The defining dynamic of How To with Jeb is the fraught, supernatural tension between Jeb and his co-host:

The Wooden Board (Jeb’s Dad): Jeb’s father is deceased, but his consciousness actively animates and speaks from a wooden board kept in the shop (“My dad knows the wood because he’s dead and he’s in it”). The board is vocal, cantankerous, and deeply dismissive of Jeb, calling him “a mean boy, not a man.”
The Patricide Implication: Dark subtext permeates their interactions. Dialogue heavily implies that Jeb killed his father and bound his soul into the lumber, though the act has never been officially confirmed on air. The father frequently rebukes Jeb for being “sinister,” while Jeb deflects by reminding him that as wood, he needs to “get over it.”
The Father’s Work Ethic: The board dad defends his parenting by asserting he never mistreated Jeb aside from “not being around,” boasting that he only worked about four hours in his entire life because the family “mostly coasted off the inheritance I got from my father.”
Sibling Rivalry with Jet Nogget: The father openly despises Jeb while celebrating Jeb’s brother, Jet Nogget. According to both Jeb and the board, Jet was the family’s golden boy—a child prodigy who made millions developing “smart apps” by age 12 and relentlessly bragged about his fortune. Jeb harbors deep resentment toward Jet’s celebrated status.
Jeb’s New Face: After an undisclosed absence, Jeb returned to the shop wearing a face that was almost his—close enough to pass a hurried glance, wrong enough that chat and the board immediately noticed. On air he blamed a forty-foot empty-well fall and emergency reconstruction with throat tissue, after world-class plastic-surgeon brother Jet proved “too busy” to help (2025-07-01). Viewers and staff spun impostor and body-swap theories: that the original Jeb had been replaced, that someone else was wearing a near-miss face, or that the “real Jeb skin suit” had gone missing in the network crawlspaces (2026-08-14). The board dad has never confirmed which theory he prefers; he only insists this Jeb still isn’t a man.

Curriculum & Topics

Wood Splitting & Handling: Initial tutorials on axe safety, chopping blocks, and preserving blades. Jeb quickly brushes past practical demonstration, noting all his timber is pre-cut.
Practical Self-Defense: Reviewing college-level martial arts tutorials taught by instructor Daryl Morris, covering escapes from chokes, clothing grabs, headlocks, and bear hugs. Jeb pays particular attention to groin defense (“protect groin, be like a turtle”), noting the skills may be necessary if he ever has to physically fight his wooden father.
Club “Dirty Dancing” Etiquette: Instructional breakdowns on nightclub dancing, leading Jeb to attempt suggestive pelvic choreography directly on camera.

Known Occurrences

segments/hype-train.title: Hype Train
segments/hype-train.content:
Hype Train

The high-velocity musical and cultural broadcast interruption on Barely Informed News, triggered whenever network momentum reaches surge velocity.
Format
The primary news telecast is abruptly overridden by a neon-bordered synthwave landscape featuring a giant retro “HYPE” sun and horizon grid. The broadcast shifts focus to Hype Train—a sentient locomotive correspondent traveling alongside an upright black panther companion.
While officially tasked with acknowledging viewer contributions and network patrons, Hype Train routinely derails into energetic freestyle raps over live beats, which invariably veer into surreal commentary regarding bodily fluids, culinary mechanics, and existential philosophies.
Broadcast Lore & Tropes

Donor Roll Derailments: Begins reading verified network patrons before completely abandoning the queue for rapid-fire rhyming monologues.
Fluidic Inquiries: Uncontrollable thematic drift toward fluidic subjects, including storage containers, claims of being “in piss,” and his unreleased video game pitch Piss Fruit Ninja.
Freestyle Rhythms: Commands the audio console to deliver vaudeville beats, Dr. Seuss rhyming cadences, or sensual R&B grooves.
The Panther Partner: An upright panther traveling with the train whom Hype Train introduces as his non-exclusive partner.
Extradimensional Origins: Regular dispatches from Hype Train’s native dimensional plane, the “crypto universe.”

segments/jambalaya.title: Jambalaya
segments/jambalaya.content:
Jambalaya

A multi-guest “secret blank” debate panel on Barely Informed News, debuted during the 2024-07-20 eight-hour debate marathon.
Format
Jambalaya seats several network contributors and/or studio guests against an “infinite inky void” backdrop. One panelist holds a hidden trait or confession (the secret blank)—for example a secret Obama voter, secret cannibal, or secret bedwetter—while the others and chat probe with questions until the identity is exposed.
Rounds mix political trivia, culinary absurdism, and interpersonal gotchas. The format was explicitly tested as reusable machinery for future guest-heavy broadcasts, and later inspired Jambalaya-style couch debates when guests commandeer the stream deck.
Key Elements

Secret blank: One contestant conceals a designated attribute; discovery is the win condition.
Panel mix: Recurring talent (Chet, Liliana, Grandma Crumble Bottom) alongside one-off guests (Tyler, Bill, Tim).
Chat interrogation: Audience questions drive the reveal as much as on-panel sparring.
Culinary / etiquette digressions: Side debates (artichoke-as-human, potato-as-human, condiment philosophy, smut vs no smut) often outlast the secret itself.

Munch & Crum

The flagship political debate desk on Barely Informed News, featuring fiery head-to-head clashes between senior debate analysts Ralph Munchcut and Crum.
Format
Broadcast under the title Munch & Crum, the segment features rotating 3D network title cards, an automated on-screen scoreboard, and live audience referendum polling. Munch and Crum debate national policies, municipal leadership, and culinary ethics, with arguments frequently escalating into personal grievances and high-stakes wagers.
Substitutes and alters occasionally take a mic — notably Scrum (Crum’s temp/alter), Plumb (Crum’s cousin), and Al Manchester (Munch’s soft half). Some telecasts host multiple debates.

News

The flagship news desk and central broadcast block of Barely Informed News.
Format
Lead anchor Case Blackwell presides over the anchor desk in front of a panoramic Los Angeles skyline backdrop. Featuring an active illuminated desk badge and a continuous scrolling “BREAKING” news ticker along the bottom of the screen, the broadcast covers major national headlines, political developments, bizarre domestic incidents, and live viewer dispatches.
Key Elements

Lead Anchor: Case Blackwell
Visual Presentation: Studio news desk, digital globe graphics, and continuous breaking news ticker.
Tone: Deadpan satirical broadcast journalism and investigative reporting.

Rebuild Rennerton

Rebuild Rennerton is the live municipal reconstruction desk on Barely Informed News: chat-elected mayors (starting with skeletal Ralph Munchcut / Skellomunch) rebuild the ruined city of Rennerton inside a modded Valheim world while citizens grill them via !pc.
Format
Case loads Valheim as “Rennerton management software,” seats the current mayor in-character, and lets chat join the server as press / settlers. The mayor harvests, builds (mansion first, democracy later), fields !pc press questions, and occasionally executes misbehaving deer. Elections are promised once a town hall exists; until then the incumbent runs a one-skeleton municipal monopoly.
