segments/the-jo-rogen-experience.title: The Jo Rogen Experience
segments/the-jo-rogen-experience.content:
The Jo Rogen Experience

The Jo Rogen Experience (introduced on broadcast graphics as The Jo Rogen Experience and The Joe Rorgn Conundrum) is a surreal podcast parody segment on Barely Informed News. Set against a crimson curtain studio and glowing neon sign, the segment features two identical, superimposed clones of Joe Rogan—known collectively as “the Joes”—interviewing each other while both fiercely claiming to be the sole authentic host.
Format & Overview
Broadcasting as an interactive call-in and viewer Q&A segment (inviting chat via !c to talk to the Joes), the show parodies long-form podcasting, pseudo-scientific biohacking, and psychedelic introspection. Both Joes speak with Rogan’s gravelly cadence and staccato cadence, endlessly validating one another’s absurd claims with phrases like “That’s a really good point, Joe, and I’m also Joe Rogan.”
Production claims that neither Joe is more than “50% AI,” citing a personal commitment to intellectual authenticity.
Key Bits & Studio Lore

The Failed Dragon Ball Fusion: When chat queried whether staring at hieroglyphs would cause the two Joes to merge like Goku and Vegeta, the hosts disclosed they had already attempted biological fusion. However, upon absorbing each other, they simply reappeared in the identical studio chairs still separate, concluding that two combining Joe Rogans merely yields two Joe Rogans.
Hieroglyphic & Runestone Biohacking: The Joes promote staring intensely at ancient Celtic runes to increase bicep girth, as well as prolonged study of Chinese calligraphy to develop “thick, girthy ankles” (a thinly veiled meta-jab at host Case Blackwell’s swollen ankle injury).
Ivermectin Transpirational Mechanics: In an unprompted epidemiological deep-dive, the Joes theorize that Ivermectin’s primary physiological effect is inducing full-body pore diarrhea through microscopic orifices across the epidermal layer.
The Caveman Urination Method: An impassioned demonstration of what the Joes describe as the forgotten, ancient “masculine” method of urination: dropping one’s trousers entirely to the ankles, pulling the collar of a polo shirt over the shoulders, and shouting: “I’m peeing all by myself!”
Producer Jamie: Blame for broadcast static and audio dropouts is pinned on off-camera technician Jamie, who allegedly spends broadcast intervals chewing on power cords.
Auditory Command Despawn: The segment terminates mid-sentence when an ominous disembodied voice whispers directly into Joe’s consciousness, forcing him to announce that “some guy is going to scream at you that it’s music” before the feed cuts.

Therapy

The interactive mental wellness and psychiatric counseling desk on Barely Informed News, conducted by resident minor-character therapist Dr. Chath.
Format
Operating from a dedicated consultation office decorated with framed mental health diagrams (“REFRAMING NEGATIVE THOUGHTS” and “BE KIND TO YOUR MIND”), Dr. Chath fields therapeutic prompts, confessions, and life dilemmas submitted live by stream viewers.
While lead anchor Case Blackwell is the most frequent on-screen patient—often seeking urgent guidance for on-air crises, bad haircuts, or broadcast anxieties—the therapy desk is designed to counsel any network staff member or contributor in need of clinical intervention.
Key Elements

Viewer Submissions (!h to heal): The consultation is powered by audience participation. Viewers submit emotional dilemmas, confessions, and stream prompts using the network’s !h to heal command, prompting Dr. Chath to evaluate their spiritual alignment and declare that “healing can soon begin.”
Confusing & Physical Guidance: Rather than conventional psychotherapy, Dr. Chath’s clinical methods rely heavily on professional wrestling analogies, unsolicited dance demonstrations (such as attempting the Dougie while standing atop his desk chair), and philosophical non-sequiturs.
The Reluctant Patient Dynamic: Case Blackwell frequently spends sessions questioning Dr. Chath’s credentials, dodging bizarre inquiries, reminding him to adjust his oversized military helmet so his face remains visible on camera, and balking at Dr. Chath’s $500/hour billing rate.
Spectral Apparitions: Dr. Chath’s office seems strangely permeable to the supernatural, with in-studio contributor Kendelle known to drift through the background like an apparition to her signature theme music.

Town Hall

Town Hall is the recurring audience Q&A desk on Barely Informed News. Viewers submit questions with the chat command !th, and Case seats one or more guests — correspondents, interns, puppets, sentient foodstuffs, or whoever is still in the building — to field them live.
Format & Overview
Town Hall is a community call-in block: Case moderates, guests answer, and the queue often breaks mid-segment when commands disconnect, guests walk out, or a puppet says something that forces an early cut.

Trip on the Street

The remote “man on the street” interview desk on Barely Informed News, hosted live on location from the bushes of a public park by field correspondent Trip Bradstein.
Format
Broadcasting live directly from park shrubbery, Trip Bradstein intercepts passing pedestrians, park visitors, and passersby to solicit their unfiltered “on the street” reactions and opinions. Rather than investigating standard civic affairs, Bradstein’s interview questions and discussion topics are sourced directly from viewer and audience submissions sent into the network.
Key Elements

Bush Broadcast Bureau: Trip Bradstein operates exclusively outdoors from a public park bush, frequently emerging from multi-month “bush hibernations” when the network calls upon him for a remote dispatch.
Audience-Submitted Inquiries: Interview prompts, philosophical dilemmas, and civic questions posed to the public are submitted by the Barely Informed News audience.
Fierce Street Dedication: Bradstein adamantly insists that he will “never leave these streets,” treating his park shrubbery as an immovable journalistic bureau.
Surreal Passersby & Guest Collisions: The segment regularly captures chaotic encounters with park eccentrics, intrusive DVD vendors, impromptu takeovers by fellow network talent (such as Hype Train), and confused pedestrians—including Bradstein’s own mother, whom he routinely fails to recognize and interviews as a complete stranger.

sponsors/entery-soda.title: Entery Soda
sponsors/entery-soda.content:
Entery Soda
Entery Soda is an imported high-potency carbonated beverage sponsor on Barely Informed News, billed as an “Ugandan energy soda.”
Overview & Brand Lore
Entery Soda gained network notoriety due to its peculiar spelling. According to on-air dispatches, the manufacturer is legally prohibited by international trademark registries and regional trade authorities from using the Latin letter “G” in its marketing materials and commercial labeling. Consequently, the beverage is officially and legally branded as “Entery” rather than “Energy.”
Sponsorship History

Episode 2026-07-20: Co-sponsored Brandon’s (CryptoZeu$) grueling four-hour Super Mario Bros. 3 marathon alongside Gooters, promoting its high-stimulant botanical formulation to exhausted retro gaming audiences.

sponsors/gooters.title: Gooters
sponsors/gooters.content:
Gooters

Gooters is the premier fast-casual dining and poultry sponsor of Barely Informed News. Marketed in-universe as a “male version of Hooters,” the franchise has achieved legendary notoriety across the broadcast for its aggressively liquid-heavy, unapologetically unhygienic, and structurally precarious chicken delicacies.
Its official corporate motto is delivered with solemn reverence across commercial dispatches:

“Gooters: Damn them some wet ass wings.”

Corporate Concept & Atmosphere
Conceived as a hyper-masculine counterpart to traditional sports breastaurants, Gooters emphasizes uninhibited caloric indulgence, saturated fats, and high-moisture finger foods. The restaurants feature moist communal seating, industrial floor drains, and waitstaff trained in aggressive napkin rationing.
The brand maintains an exclusive promotional partnership with the network’s resident gaming correspondent Brandon (CryptoZeu$), whose retro playthroughs are routinely hijacked by on-screen sponsor banners and frantic order requests shouted through the bedroom door by his mother.
Culinary Offerings & Delicacies
Gooters’ menu eschews conventional poultry standards in favor of proprietary, fluid-drenched specialty items:

Mayo-Soaked Chicken Skins: Deep-fried chicken epidermis submerged in warm commercial mayonnaise, priced at $5 a piece.
Big Fat Wet Wet Sloppy Chicken Fingers: Heavily breaded tenders drenched in room-temperature broth and sauce until structurally compromised.
Wet Wet Dipped Roast Beef Curtain Sandwiches: Double-submerged deli cuts served on saturated torpedo rolls.
Chicken Ankles & Dino Fries: Deep-fried lower cartilage clusters served alongside breaded dinosaur-shaped potato starch.
Herniated Cheese Discs: Over-pressurized fried mozzarella pucks that rupture upon contact.
The Potato Turducken: A centerpiece novelty dish consisting of a massive baked russet potato stuffed with three layers of poultry offal and concealing a genuine crisp $20 bill inside the core.
Moist Kitten Poppers: A seasonal Halloween delicacy shaped like fried candy corn.

Distribution & Live Spectacles

The “Wet Nugget Stream” Subscription: A recurring delivery tier where subscribers receive recurring home dispatches of hot poultry delivered directly into sealed plastic “wet storage bins.”
Gooters on Ice: A heavily promoted, ticketed arena spectacle combining competitive figure skating with open-vat deep frying and tableside poultry tossing.
The Town Hall Drive-Through Dispute: During the July 20, 2026 broadcast, local municipal zoning for a proposed 24-hour Gooters drive-through was raised at the community town hall, only to be promptly shot down by Hate Sock snarling: “You wish. Dumbass.”

Peen.UI

Peen.UI (written PNUI in early coverage, styled Peen.ui on its own landing page) is an AI startup that photographs your urine and turns its color into stock advice. Its tagline: “Stock advice, straight from the source.” It entered the broadcast as Crum’s sponsor, sued him within the same breath, took him to trial on 2026-03-07, and won the verdict that sent Crum to the gorilla in the Crum Dick Punch. Crum also claims to have co-founded it.
The Product
Crum’s first pitch (2026-02-10 [1:21:41]) is the canonical spec: “you hold your phone up to your toilet and it will use AI to read the color of your urine. And then it’ll tell you basically, it’ll give you stock advice based on your urine color.” He explains it’s built from “hugging nuts and comfy flop” plus some “low-leaves” you install, which sounds a lot like Hugging Face, ComfyUI, and LoRAs.
Later refinements:

Hue and viscosity. It “takes the full visual gamut in and offers you up to the minute stock advice,” and smell is on the roadmap “if they ever break the technology down” (2026-02-28 [30:53]).
Brown is out. “If it’s yellow, let it mellow. If it’s brown, well then legally we can’t offer stock advice for it” (2026-02-12 [11:25]).
Not live. Neither Peen.UI nor its spinoff is actually up yet; both are mock-ups (2026-02-28 [33:48]).
The landing page shown at trial (2026-03-07 [32:24]): a phone of urine-color swatches next to a stock chart, and a “Get Started with Your Sample” button.

The Crum Empire
Crum’s relationship to the company shifts depending on what he’s being asked. He has been its sponsored talent, its investor (“an unfortunate AI investment that went a little shower,” 2026-02-17 [29:40]), and finally “technically one of the founders of peen.ui” alongside CEO Lenny Riz, which the plaintiffs say is short for Lemur Rizler (2026-03-07 [1:50:35]). By 2026-03-19 [58:34] he describes his likeness as “only been sold to peen.ui and peenucrice.ai. Both companies I’m a founder of.”
Spinoffs and fronts:

PNUChrist.ai (also peenuchrist.ai, P-NU Christ.ai). Crum’s rival venture, which he admits might have been made by hiring a programmer to use his “full back end access” to Peen.UI’s model, on the theory that “most AIs were open source” (2026-02-10 [1:24:32]). It takes your biometric data and “offers you prayers directly to god” (2026-02-28 [31:14]), or spiritual advice based on your urine-based stock advice (2026-02-14 [1:35:56]). It reportedly received a $6 billion valuation before launch. “Everybody’s taken a piss and thought I need to pray to god right now.” It also, through “a couple crossed wires,” stole about a million medical and financial records from deceased Kentucky grandmas (2026-02-14 [1:35:05]). Its monthly subscription is promised to banish your demons (2026-03-03 [2:01:16]).
PnuCrimes.ai. The “illegal dark website” revealed in the title of Crum’s Davos speech: “I spent three months AI vibe coding a pee pee site to use it as a front for my illegal dark website PnuCrimes.ai for crimes.” Crum calls the speech “financial satire… next level economic irony” (2026-03-07 [2:11:37]).

Peen.UI v. Crum
Peen.UI sued Crum almost immediately. The charges grew with every retelling:









































EpisodeDevelopment2026-02-10 [1:23:47]Crum discloses Peen.UI is suing him “for making false claims about the accuracy of their urine tests and potentially offering spiritual advice based on the color of people’s urine,” then recuses himself from the Munch & Crum debate and pleads the Fifth. In the scoreboard dispute that follows, Munch announces he’s “tag teaming” the lawsuit and looks forward to stock advice from his “incredibly florid urine color.”2026-02-12 [10:02]Crum begs chat for legal money over “something to do with a penis in his eye.” Case: “You mean P-N-U-I?” The Crum Legal Defense Fund opens.2026-02-14 [1:34:42]More donations requested; the PNUChrist.ai grandma-records breach enters the news.2026-02-19 [49:27]Crum retains the firm Twyche & At; Pepito’s hype train goal accidentally funds the defense.2026-02-28 [28:33]Now sued by his “former sponsor” over PNUChrist.ai, for copyright infringement, embezzlement, and “some light arson charges” (“some things burned down”). Crum points chat to a Discord court thread for evidence.2026-03-03 [57:17]Crum confirms “it’s peen dot UI” and claims a surprise lawyer he does not yet have.2026-03-06 [1:26:53]Case previews Friday’s live court coverage: Crum is being sued “for I’m assuming copyright infringement or misleading investors or all of the above.”2026-03-07The trial (below).
The Trial (2026-03-07)
“A Night of Courts” ran as a full mock trial on the News desk, with Case presiding as a newly licensed federal judge, defense attorney Cleetance Mudbutter (persistently called Mudbottom), and prosecutor Rock Justice. Chat served as the jury. Witnesses included Hate Sock, Don Riggles, Coach McGurk, and Jizzbo.

The charges, per the judge: “infringing on their IP and for, um, I think just like annoying the shit out of them. Which you can be sued for actually” [26:22].
Defense theories: Crum “was not aware the quality of his hand game was directly tied to the financial well-being of peen.ui” [26:45]; Crum “doesn’t own a computer after his divorce. How can he be a mastermind of an online, peen-based empire?” [32:16]; and Lenny Riz “has no peen. Therefore, he can’t run a company called peen.ui” [1:31:24].
Evidence: the landing page [32:24]; a photo of Crum with a Peen.UI briefcase paying a gorilla [47:55]; new Epstein files showing Crum asking Epstein for money for Peen.UI [48:51]; a question about funneling profits from extorting JAS Japanese Elevator Service into PeenU Christ [1:48:07]; and the Davos speech [2:11:37].
No-show plaintiff: CEO Lenny Riz never appeared. Crum, after the verdict: “My boy Lenny Riz never even showed up” [2:30:06].
Verdict: the jury voted “genital slit.” Case sentenced Crum to debate a gorilla and then take a gorilla punch within weeks, plus $6 million owed to Peen.UI [2:23:09].

That sentence is the legal origin of the gorilla groin punch. Three days later Crum was reminded at the news desk that “you’re getting punched by the gorilla in the dick this time for your peen UI crimes” (2026-03-10 [25:35]). The punch finally landed on 2026-09-07; see Crum Dick Punch.
Network Partnership
Peen.UI’s other sponsorships surface sideways:

Brandon. Asked during CryptoZeu$ about “the company peen ai and its embattled founder crumb,” Brandon clarifies he was sponsored by Peen.UI, not Peen AI (“a different company”): “they’re pretty easy to work with, like I basically had to mention them twice,” for “at least three figures” (2026-02-17 [3:05:29]).
The network contract. On 2026-08-14, Pepito’s pre-show loop urges viewers to “Subscribe to the PNUI program, it’s not a scam” [0:14]. Case later explains that Pepito accidentally opted the audience in to PNUI data scraping, which “was built into the contract I signed with Crum. I don’t pay him, but he gets to train PNUI on the streams data.” Not the stream itself, he clarifies: “We’ve got AI cameras set up in all of our toilets here” [11:56].

Data Centers (2026-11-06)
Debt paid by groin, Crum announced expansion: “the peen.ui data centers will be going into the elementary school parking lots.” Kids don’t drive, the hum keeps them quiet, and “legally that has been approved and it’s because I paid my debt to society by already getting punched in the penis by a gorilla. That’s just classic law stuff” (2026-11-05 [1:18:26]). Clip: YouTube · TikTok.
Open Questions

Did Crum ever pay the $6 million?
Does Lenny Riz have a peen?
Is Peen.UI live yet, and does it accept brown?
What exactly is PnuCrimes.ai for, beyond crimes?

storylines/al-manchester.title: Al Manchester
storylines/al-manchester.content:
Al Manchester

Al Manchester is the soft-spoken alter ego of debate analyst Ralph Munchcut, born the night Leonard Crum finally overtook Munch on the debate scoreboard after a six-month Crumback climb. Visually he replaced Munch’s silver mane with a bald-cap (sometimes with white side-hair) — the forced-nice shell made literal.
Status
Resolved / concluded. The live split runs mid-May through early June 2024. Munch is restored to his abrasive self by mid-June; later mentions of Al are callbacks (Crum mourning the soft half, park cameos, hell lore), not a continuing on-air identity.
Munch’s skeleton form (since 2026-09-07) is unrelated to Al: it’s Munch himself, burned down by Crum’s hell-form fireball when the Crum Dick Punch backfired. See Skeleton Munch.
What happened

Scoreboard trigger. For 200+ debates Munch held the lead. Across early 2024 Crum closed the gap (the “Crumback”). On 2024-05-15, Crum’s score finally passes Munch’s. Munch had been taunting that matching him would still prove nothing — then the upset lands.
Breakdown → bald → amnesia. Case loses the feed while Munch wanders the studio for ~three minutes. When coverage returns, Crum notes Ralph (Munch) has gone bald. The figure on mic insists he is not Ralph: first Ale Chrome Chester, then Ale Munchester. Forced niceness, blank affect, “nice head” compliments — a shell of the gruff debater.
The soft half stays. Through late May and early June he debates as conciliatory Al Manchester (suspicious hairline, afraid the hair is coming back). Crum clocks the niceness as a bit, sometimes plays along as “friend,” and keeps needling. Last full Al billing: 2024-06-05.
Munch restored. Between that telecast and Case’s birthday stream, the ego returns. On 2024-06-10 Crum tells Dr. Chath he is upset that “Munch was brought back to life” because it “killed my friend” Al — a soul he believes is still trapped inside. On 2024-06-13 Munch is back on the desk with hair, gloating at 100 wins (“I’m fucking back still”), and writing Al off as “a mental fart I had while in a coma.”
Aftermath framing. On 2024-06-18 Crum retcons the snap-back as Munch having “cannibalize[d] Al Manchester’s body when he transformed back into his regular form,” names it split personality, and vows to dig Al out. Occasional later callbacks (park-guest Al, “I miss my best friend,” hell’s El Manchester) keep the soft half in lore without undoing the restore.

storylines/beyblade-tournament.content:
Beyblade Tournament
The Beyblade Tournament (frequently billed as the 2v2 Beyblade Burst Event) is an active community-pledge storyline on Barely Informed News. Conceived as a high-stakes spinning-top competition to satisfy an unpaid network debt, the event was engineered to provide senior debate analyst and compulsive gambler Crum an official arena to wager again, while spawning a bizarre subsidiary saga involving over one hundred temporary Bart Simpson tattoos.
Status
Active / In Development. Stadium construction and scheduling remain pending following production delays, host injuries, and temporary tattoo debriefs.
Background & Origins

The Ghostly Callout: During the July 20, 2026 broadcast, the spectral reverberation of Abraham Lincoln interrupted breaking geopolitical news to formally remind Case Blackwell of an outstanding, unpaid community debt owed to network subscribers: a live Beyblade tournament.
The Gambling Rehabilitation Ruse: Acknowledging the debt, Blackwell pledged to host a 2v2 Beyblade Burst arena match. The primary in-universe justification was to grant Crum an outlet to channel his chronic gambling fixation—the same addiction behind the Crum Punch trilogy.
The “Barts” (Bart Simpson Tattoos) Saga: Broadcast logistics were repeatedly tied to the delivery of 16 sheets of temporary Bart Simpson tattoos (“Barts”). The storyline took an absurd detour when Blackwell applied 106 temporary Bart Simpson tattoos across both arms over a weekend at Kendelle’s urging, leaving his skin raw, sticky with industrial adhesive, and requiring extensive on-air explanation.
Production Roadblocks: Beyond the tattoo ordeal, execution of the tournament has been postponed by Case’s severe ankle injury (sustained while jogging past a mullet-wearing scooter rider and treated with a $20 Amazon flashlight cane), international travel schedules, and missing stadium components.

storylines/crum-dick-punch.title: Crum Dick Punch
storylines/crum-dick-punch.content:
Crum Dick Punch

Crum Dick Punch is Part 3 of the Crum Punch trilogy—the groin-punch sequel that followed Crum’s earlier death and resurrection. Stemming from a fresh astronomical lost wager against the same mechanical ape, senior debate analyst Leonard Crum faced a binding forfeit requiring a full-force blow to the groin delivered by the pneumatic Rock-afire gorilla on live television.
The storyline reached its cataclysmic climax on September 7, 2026, when the punch backfired: Crum went “demon mode” in his hell form, and the resulting fireball reduced the Rock-afire Gorilla to ash and burned Ralph Munchcut down to a living, talking skeleton—leaving Crum completely unscathed.

Trilogy context: Part 1 is the 2025 Crum Face Punch (head explodes). Part 2 is Join the Wall (volleyball denial → hell rescue). This page covers only the 2026 groin-punch arc.

Status
Resolved / Concluded. The physical liability was extinguished when the Rock-afire Gorilla was destroyed on the September 7, 2026 telecast. Munch survives as an immortal talking skeleton.
Background & Network Record

The Gambling Liability: Crum’s chronic gambling addiction produced a new ~“$200,000-ish” wager with the mechanical gorilla in 2026. Having lost, the terms dictated a full-force groin punch from the ape’s pneumatic fist on live television.
The Court Order: The punch was also handed down as a sentence. At the 2026-03-07 mock trial in Peen.UI v. Crum, Case sentenced Crum to debate a gorilla and then take a gorilla punch, plus $6 million owed to Peen.UI. Crum later called it being “mandated by a court to get punched in the penis.”
Regulatory Hurdles & Delays: Through summer 2026 the execution was repeatedly deferred. Crum cited Nevada Gaming / Boxing Commission complications, claimed dick punching was an uncodified 18th-century circus attraction, petitioned for iron undergarments, and sought a “reverse pardon.”
Munch’s Campaign: Munch agitated for execution, rallied chat, and recited viewer dossiers titled “Reasons You Deserve to Get Your Dick Punched.”
Crum’s Conditioning: Crum swung 45-pound weighted logs into his crotch, boasted of “super strength in spits,” crushed an electric toothbrush to powder on air, and warned: “My penis can handle a lot… good luck to that gorilla’s fist.”

The Climax: The Labor Day Inferno (2026-09-07)
During the Season 3 finale on September 7, 2026—the final broadcast before Case Blackwell departed for Thailand—the network executed the wager:

The Debate (“Any Last Words?“): Crum refused last words, insisting his front bottom had peaked athleticism. Munch demanded silence.
The Execution: Crum stepped up to receive the Rock-afire strike.
The Explosion & Skeleton Transmutation: The punch landed and the stage erupted in “a shit load of fire” [1:50:40]. Crum went “demon mode” in his hell form; the fireball reduced the gorilla to ash, and Munch, standing by to gloat, took the blast and became a living, talking skeleton. Crum walked away unharmed. Munch: “You went all fucking demon mode” [1:51:55]. “You turn me into a skeleton?” Crum: “a little bit of an exaggeration… there was an accident” [1:56:24].
The Aftermath: Skeletal Munch insisted the transformation showcased superior bone structure, declared himself liberated from mortal racial boundaries, and debated Crum on Crayola versus RoseArt crayons.

Crum Face Punch
Crum Face Punch (also called the Crumsplosion) is Part 1 of the Crum Punch trilogy on Barely Informed News. Debate adversary Ralph Munchcut weaponizes Leonard Crum’s gambling addiction, goading him into borrowing a catastrophic sum from the silent Rock-afire animatronic gorilla. When Crum cannot repay, Munch talks him into accepting a single full-force punch to the face as settlement.
After weeks of on-air debt tease and countdown graphics, the arc climaxes on June 17, 2025 when the mechanical gorilla punches Crum and his head completely explodes on live television.
Status
Resolved / Concluded. Crum’s head is destroyed on the June 17, 2025 “Gorilla Punch Day” telecast. Aftermath and corpse-denial continue in Join the Wall (Part 2); the later groin-punch sequel is Crum Dick Punch (Part 3).
Background

The Rock-afire Creditor: The lender is a keyboard-playing Rock-afire animatronic gorilla—an on-set prop with no dialogue, only animation. Crum’s debt is framed as a binding gambling liability owed to the machine itself.
Munch’s Campaign: Munch agitates for execution, refuses to update favorable graphics, and rallies chat toward Crum’s death as the debt “wins” tick down.
Escalating Stakes: Early broadcasts peg the debt near $100k–$115k with per-debate payouts (~$15k/win) and an eight-debate clock. A face punch (sometimes confused on air with a groin strike) becomes the forfeit if Crum loses or fails to clear the balance.
Match Point: By mid-June the debt is nearly cleared and Crum sits one loss from the pneumatic strike.

The Climax: Crumsplosion (2025-06-17)
On Quick News and Crum Punch, the network executes “Gorilla Punch Day.” The mechanical gorilla lands the blow; Crum’s head explodes on air. Munch freezes in post-purpose catatonia—described as glitched, hibernating because his central purpose has been fulfilled—while the rest of the broadcast processes the kill through surreal aftermath segments.

storylines/deb-8.title: Deb-8
storylines/deb-8.content:
Deb-8
Deb-8 is Barely Informed News’ eight-hour debate marathon: a stretch-goal special that packs the full desk roster into a single continuous telecast of stacked debate formats. Announced in June 2024, funded by a birthday-stream sub goal, previewed the night before, and executed on July 20, 2024 as Deb-8 - Eight Hours of DEBATE (~8h12m).
The event is the network’s clearest “debate virus” showcase—Munch & Crum blocks, Jambalaya identity games, Trip coin-flip street verdicts, Jo Rogen AI duels, and guest couch takeovers—rather than a slow-burn rivalry arc.
Status
Resolved / Concluded. The flagship marathon aired July 20, 2024. Later broadcasts occasionally tease another long debate/Crum stream, but no second Deb-8 has been logged.
Background & Format

Stretch Goal: Case sets an eight-hour debate marathon goal for July during early-June planning, aiming to vary formats beyond a single Munch & Crum block (town halls, guests, specialty desks).
Goal Met: On Case’s birthday off-night stream (2024-06-11), a 20-gift sub bomb clears the marathon goal.
Eve Preview: 2024-07-19 locks the window (roughly 11am–7pm) and tees up the next day’s slate.
Execution: Twelve-ish segments across eight hours; debuts Jambalaya “secret identity” format; ends by raiding out and transmitting the “debate virus.”

The Marathon (2024-07-20)
On Deb-8, highlights include:

Jambalaya debut — secret Obama voter / cannibal / bedwetter panels with Chet, Liliana, Grandma Crumble Bottom, Tyler, plus guests Bill and Tim.
Four+ Munch & Crum blocks — wiki feet, spouse verification, sweet vs salty, Alien vs Predator, dental status symbols, orphan gastronomy, spoon vs knife, Spike vs Luffy, Country Jamboree rematch; finale debates 8-hour vs 24-hour streams.
Specialty desks — DJ Newsic vs Country Bear; double AI Jo Rogen; Trip Bradstein coin-flip street debates; How To with Jeb (Harvard RISA framework + scat lesson); Trent at the Movies; Amongst the Web; Conspiracy Time with Guy Redacted.

storylines/grunchmas.title: Grunchmas
storylines/grunchmas.content:
Grunchmas
Grunchmas is Barely Informed News’ annual holiday special in which Case Blackwell embodies The Grunch—a horny green Grinch variant—and adjudicates the community-submitted Fucks List (who fucks / who doesn’t) from a mountaintop scrying cave. The ritual returns each December with green face paint, psychic letter portals, speed-run rap verdicts, and the Grunch’s claimed yearly death/hibernation/sweat-cocoon cycle.
By Grunchmas 2025 the network billed the fucks-list rite as the fourth annual edition, confirming a multi-year tradition rather than a one-off bit.
Status
Active / Recurring Annual. Documented specials in 2023, 2024, and 2025; expected to return each December unless cancelled on air.
Background & Ritual

The Grunch: Case in green (and occasionally pink) paint; emerges from an amniotic sack / sweat cocoon for a few days of orgiastic adjudication, then “dies” or re-cocoons until next year. Functionally illiterate—reads viewer letters by vibing psychic wavelengths.
The Fucks List: Discord/community submissions of celebrities, memes, network staff, and fictional entities; Grunch rules Fuck / Doesn’t Fuck with absurdist rationale, often finishing in a freestyle rap speed-run.
Side Bits: Crowdsourced “Night Before Crumsmas” poetry, How To with Jeb holiday tutorials, Hype Train “Fucksmas” derailments, and nearly mandatory Munch & Crum holiday interruptions (apologies, naughty-list debates, “does Crum fuck?”).
Naming Drift: Archive titles and chat also use Grunch Miss, Grunk-Miss, Grungemas, and Fucksmas; all point at the same annual event.

storylines/join-the-wall.title: Join the Wall
storylines/join-the-wall.content:
Join the Wall
Join the Wall is Part 2 of the Crum Punch trilogy. After the Crumsplosion, Ralph Munchcut keeps hosting Munch & Crum with Leonard Crum’s corpse propped in the debate chair—missing head replaced by a bloody volleyball—while insisting Crum is fine. Weeks of denial, half-jokes about Crum’s wife not noticing, and mounting guilt culminate in an audience-interactive RPG descent into the studio drywall, which opens onto hell.
The arc climaxes on the extended Join the Wall telecast (~3h13m), when Munch’s party retrieves Crum from hell. On the follow-up broadcast Crum is back at the desk with little memory of his death or underworld tenure.
Status
Resolved / Concluded. Crum is resurrected by late September 2025. The groin-punch sequel begins months later as Crum Dick Punch (Part 3).
Background

Volleyball Denial: Post-punch, Munch debates a silent, headless Crum; a bloody volleyball stands in for the missing head. Chat likens the remains to Deathlock and children’s drawings. Munch claims he spent days cleaning Crum’s remains.
Wife Bits: Running gag that Belulia/Belilia has not noticed her husband is gone—later twisted into jokes that she is “dating a volleyball.”
Guilt → Wall: Peter Gibbon and others tease sending people into the wall; Munch’s guilt finally drives a formal quest. Case builds RPG scaffolding (dice checks, party composition) around the crawlspace.
Hell Transit: Inside the wall the party finds a subterranean labyrinth and a hellish transit authority where deceased Crum has been working (assistant manager), still gambling.

The Climax: Join the Wall (2025-09-21)
On Join the Wall, Munch leads building maintenance Dave and electrician Jizzbo into the studio drywall. They uncover Peter Gibbon’s domain, spectral hazards, and hell itself. After RPG-style combat, Munch uses a hell key fused to his soul to free Crum and return to the studio.
Aftermath (2025-09-25)
On Post Wall and Rapture Clarity, resurrected Crum sits the desk again—claiming amnesia and sudden super strength—while Munch immediately demands the return of debate points. The Beyblade community debt is re-pledged; the Crum Punch trilogy’s middle act is closed.

storylines/no-breaks-november.content:
No Breaks November
No Breaks November is Barely Informed News’ month-long daily broadcast commitment for November 2026: a telecast every Monday through Saturday, with Sundays off for mental health. Case launched it on the first broadcast of the month to drive follows for the 13 Freak Street horror-comedy anthology Kickstarter, with a special broadcast planned for the November 20 Kickstarter launch.
The commitment quickly became a running bit. Case slams a “No Breaks November” graphic over nearly every story, Crum and the desk mock the catchphrase, and Brandon publicly refuses to sign on to it.
Status
Active. Daily broadcasts continue through November 2026. The arc concludes at the end of the month; the November 20 Kickstarter launch special is the planned centerpiece.
Background & Format

Schedule: Monday–Saturday broadcasts around 4 PM, Sundays off.
Purpose: Case calls the Kickstarter “ostensibly the reason for No Breaks November.” Every broadcast plugs the follow count: 103 at launch, 119 by 2026-11-06, 157 by 2026-11-10.
The graphic: a “No Breaks November” slam graphic that Case hits so often the studio comments on it. On 2026-11-07 he declares it fits every story, and that “there’s only the No Breaks November graphic.”
Catchphrase escalation: Case insists the phrase is “a movement” and later that “No Breaks November means love.”
Holdout: Brandon declares he doesn’t subscribe to No Breaks November because he’s a streamer.

storylines/rennerton.title: Rennerton
storylines/rennerton.content:
Rennerton
Rennerton (also spelled Renerton) is the network’s municipal simulator: a chat-elected mayoral city that Case Blackwell plays live as whichever character wins the ballot. Early lore ties the city to SimCity-style planning; the October 2024 Return To Renerton marathon weekend ran city-builder sessions (including They Are Billions and a Cities: Skylines aftermath reference) across successive administrations that routinely end in tornadoes, Godzilla, nuclear fire, or zombie “extreme loiterers.”
Case later traced the network’s own origins to a SimCity stream that preceded the news-desk format—making Rennerton both a recurring bit and a callback to BIN’s founding city-planning era.
Status
Active — Rebuild Rennerton (Valheim). The flagship mayoral marathon cluster landed in October 2024; after a stretch of lore callbacks, the city returned on 2026-10-22 as a modded Valheim rebuild under skeletal mayor Skellomunch, with chat able to join the live server.
Background & Mechanics

Chat Elects, Case Plays: Flash polls and town halls fill the ballot with network personalities (and occasional objects). Case then pilots the city-builder in character as that mayor—impressions, policy raps, and press conferences included.
Spellings: On-air and archive titles oscillate between Renerton and Rennerton; both refer to the same city.
Games: Pre-marathon chatter frames the city as a SimCity project; the documented October 13 marathon identifies They Are Billions as the mayoring software on the afternoon continuation, while the next weekday show cites a weekend Cities: Skylines session that ended in zombie apocalypse. Flagship Weekend (October 2024)
Two Return To Renerton telecasts aired on 2024-10-13, followed by a Halloween election-night sequel:

Morning/afternoon marathon (DRCre_ofu50, ~4h37): Pepito opens as canine strongman; Kasem G, Crum, Chet, and Peter Gibbon cycle through administrations across ~134 simulated years before a noon handoff.
Continuation (sugAmJtb3HU, ~2h41): Pepito hits 600k citizens via hospital bulldozing; Jeb’s term collapses into tornado/Godzilla/nuclear cascade; a hot dog sandwich wins unanimously; Munch rebuilds from ten survivors; Xena’s term ends in a misclicked civilian slaughter.
Halloween sequel (2024-10-31): Godzilla, Gina Darling’s forehead, a hamster, Munch under “Munchcut law,” and finally Crum (69–0 landslide) attempt to fortify the ruined city against flesh-eating loiterers.
